nodes.name: Client
nodes.summary: JSON-RPC client implementing engine.Backend over a reader/writer transport with pending calls, notifications and capabilities.

nodes.name: code_diagnostics.go
nodes.summary: Server-side code diagnostics RPC: negotiates the host identity at initialize, dispatches diagnostics methods, and queues ordered diagnostics event notifications.

nodes.name: initializeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Computes the remote diagnostics host identity at initialize and advertises diagnostics capabilities.

nodes.name: dispatchDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Decodes and dispatches code diagnostics RPC methods to the backend, routing live methods separately.

nodes.name: notifyDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Admits a diagnostics event into the ordered notification queue, closing the connection on exhaustion.

nodes.name: diagnosticsWriter
nodes.summary: Background writer that sends queued diagnostics notifications.

nodes.name: expireDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Detaches diagnostics attachments owned by the connection when it ends.

nodes.name: code_diagnostics_bounds.go
nodes.summary: Bounds code diagnostics results before they are sent over RPC.

nodes.name: boundDiagnosticsResult
nodes.summary: Rejects diagnostics results that exceed size bounds before sending.

nodes.name: code_diagnostics_client.go
nodes.summary: Client-side code diagnostics and live document RPC calls, gated by negotiated capabilities, with size bounds, error code normalization and notification decoding.

nodes.name: CodeDiagnosticsHostID
nodes.summary: Returns the remote diagnostics host identity negotiated at initialize.

nodes.name: diagnosticsCall
nodes.summary: Capability-checked diagnostics RPC call with error normalization.

nodes.name: normalizeDiagnosticsError
nodes.summary: Restores stable diagnostics error codes that FromRPCError mapped onto sentinels.

nodes.name: AttachCodeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Attaches code diagnostics for a project directory on the remote host.

nodes.name: AttachCodeDiagnosticsWithout
nodes.summary: Attaches with disabled languages, sending them only to servers that support codeDiagnosticsLanguages.

nodes.name: DetachCodeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Detaches a remote diagnostics attachment.

nodes.name: GetCodeDiagnosticsSnapshot
nodes.summary: Fetches a diagnostics snapshot for an attachment.

nodes.name: ApproveCodeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Approves diagnostics for a project with a mode and fingerprint.

nodes.name: RevokeCodeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Revokes diagnostics approval for an attachment.

nodes.name: RunCodeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Starts selected diagnostics checks remotely.

nodes.name: CancelCodeDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Cancels running diagnostics checks remotely.

nodes.name: diagnosticsNotification
nodes.summary: Decodes a diagnostics event notification and tracks ownership.

nodes.name: liveCall
nodes.summary: Checks the liveCodeDiagnostics capability and size bounds before sending a live document call.

nodes.name: OpenCodeDiagnosticDocument
nodes.summary: Opens a live document on the remote diagnostics host.

nodes.name: ChangeCodeDiagnosticDocument
nodes.summary: Sends a live document change to the remote host.

nodes.name: SaveCodeDiagnosticDocument
nodes.summary: Reports a live document save to the remote host.

nodes.name: CloseCodeDiagnosticDocument
nodes.summary: Closes a live document on the remote host.

nodes.name: NavigateCode
nodes.summary: Requests remote code navigation and validates the answer matches the request and bounds.

nodes.name: ReadNavigationFile
nodes.summary: Reads a remote navigation target file and validates path, limits and read-only status.

nodes.name: InvalidateCodeDiagnosticsPath
nodes.summary: Asks the remote host to invalidate diagnostics for a changed path.

nodes.name: code_diagnostics_live.go
nodes.summary: Server dispatch for live document diagnostics methods, rejecting oversized document text by decoded and escaped size before reaching the engine.

nodes.name: dispatchLiveDiagnostics
nodes.summary: Dispatches live document and navigation RPC methods to the backend.

nodes.name: errors.go
nodes.summary: JSON-RPC error codes, stable application error codes and sentinels, plus two-way mapping between Go errors and ResponseError objects.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Formats a ResponseError with its application code.

nodes.name: ToRPCError
nodes.summary: Maps Go errors and sentinels to JSON-RPC ResponseError codes.

nodes.name: FromRPCError
nodes.summary: Maps a ResponseError back to Go sentinel or typed errors.

nodes.name: ErrorData
nodes.summary: Machine-readable application code attached to a JSON-RPC error.

nodes.name: ResponseError
nodes.summary: JSON-RPC 2.0 error object with code, message and data.

nodes.name: server.go
nodes.summary: JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio Server wrapping an engine.Backend: initialize handshake with env allowlist, concurrent request handling, idle timeout, and the big method dispatch table including terminal scripts.

nodes.name: NewServer
nodes.summary: Wraps a backend with JSON-RPC stdio transport.

nodes.name: SetStarter
nodes.summary: Makes initialize build the backend with a Starter.

nodes.name: SetIdleTimeout
nodes.summary: Sets the idle timeout after which Serve returns when no frames arrive.

nodes.name: Notify
nodes.summary: Sends a JSON-RPC notification to the client.

nodes.name: Serve
nodes.summary: Reads and processes frames until EOF, cancellation or idle timeout, then waits for in-flight handlers.

nodes.name: sendResult
nodes.summary: Writes a JSON-RPC result, falling back to an error on encoding failure.

nodes.name: handleInitialize
nodes.summary: Handles the initialize request, applying allowlisted env overrides and building the backend.

nodes.name: initialize
nodes.summary: Builds the backend via starter/preparer and assembles capabilities, roots and diagnostics identity for the handshake result.

nodes.name: handleRequest
nodes.summary: Runs one request in its own context, bounds diagnostics results and sends result or error.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Large method switch decoding params and calling the matching engine.Backend method for every RPC method.

nodes.name: terminalScript
nodes.summary: Builds a launch command and renders the terminal or panel script for it.

nodes.name: Close
nodes.summary: Closes the server.

nodes.name: Server
nodes.summary: JSON-RPC stdio server state: backend, transport, in-flight handlers, starter and diagnostics ownership.

nodes.name: terminalLauncher
nodes.summary: Interface for building agent resume, new session and handoff launch commands.

nodes.name: terminal_file.go
nodes.summary: Engine method that resolves a path printed in the terminal panel to a file on the backend host, authorizing it only against registered workspace roots or catalog session cwd/repo roots.

nodes.name: ResolveTerminalFile
nodes.summary: Resolves a terminal-relative or absolute path into a files.TerminalFile, picking the most specific authorized workspace or session root and refusing non-regular files or paths outside known roots.

nodes.name: add.go
nodes.summary: Copies an uploaded local file into a missing project leaf using rooted directory handles, identity checks and exclusive creation so links cannot redirect the write and existing entries are never overwritten.

nodes.name: Add
nodes.summary: Copies a regular source file into a new project path under the edit policy and save lock, verifying parent identities and removing the partial file on failure.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Context-aware Read on addReader that aborts the copy once the request context is cancelled.

nodes.name: OpenAddSource
nodes.summary: Opens an upload source only after rejecting symlinks and non-regular files, re-checking that the opened handle matches the stat.

nodes.name: blame.go
nodes.summary: Single-line git blame for the file viewer, reporting the last commit, author and summary for a working-tree line and handling ignored, untracked and uncommitted files explicitly.

nodes.name: BlameLine
nodes.summary: Blame result for one working-tree line: commit, author, time and summary, or Ignored/Not Committed Yet markers.

nodes.name: BlameFile
nodes.summary: Returns blame for one line of a file using its current on-disk contents via git blame --contents, falling back to unrecorded answers for ignored or new files.

nodes.name: unrecordedBlame
nodes.summary: Answers blame for files Git cannot blame (ignored, untracked or staged additions absent from HEAD) without masking real git failures.

nodes.name: parseBlameLine
nodes.summary: Parses git blame --porcelain output for one line into a BlameLine.

nodes.name: blameGit
nodes.summary: Runs git for blame with a timeout and hidden console, preserving stderr in actionable errors.

nodes.name: create_directory.go
nodes.summary: Creates a new empty file or directory beneath an existing project directory under the save lock, rejecting links below the root and never replacing existing entries.

nodes.name: CreateDirectory
nodes.summary: Creates one missing directory under rel in the project root, delegating to createEntry.

nodes.name: CreateFile
nodes.summary: Creates one missing empty file under rel in the project root, delegating to createEntry.

nodes.name: createEntry
nodes.summary: Shared implementation that validates the name and policy, opens the parent through rooted handles, checks identity and exclusively creates a file or directory.

nodes.name: delete.go
nodes.summary: Permanently deletes a project file or directory through rooted filesystem operations serialized with saves, so links cannot redirect recursive removal outside the project.

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.summary: Removes a regular file or directory tree under the edit policy, holding the save lock and verifying the parent and target identity before a rooted RemoveAll.

nodes.name: directories.go
nodes.summary: Enumerates a Git workspace's directories in bounded frontiers, asking git check-ignore before descending so ignored dependency trees are never walked.

nodes.name: walkDirectories
nodes.summary: Breadth-first directory walk that batches candidate subdirectories into bounded frontiers, decides ignore status per frontier and queues only survivors.

nodes.name: ignoredDirectories
nodes.summary: Runs git check-ignore over one frontier of anchored './path' candidates and maps the echoed answers back, avoiding pathspec magic.

nodes.name: download.go
nodes.summary: Streams a project file or a ZIP of a directory for download using rooted filesystem operations, rejecting symlinks and special files inside archives.

nodes.name: Download
nodes.summary: Describes a download artifact (name, type, size) without exposing its server-side path.

nodes.name: WriteDownload
nodes.summary: Writes the original file bytes or a ZIP archive of the selected directory to dst, walking through rooted handles and refusing links and irregular entries.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Context-aware Read on contextReader that stops streaming when the request is cancelled.

nodes.name: edit_path.go
nodes.summary: Defines EditPolicy, the host-local protection policy for project editing: metadata-only preflight checks rejecting '..', symlinks, junctions, protected credential/metadata names and configured tool store roots.

nodes.name: EditPolicy
nodes.summary: Protection policy listing protected store roots; its zero value still protects credential and repository metadata names.

nodes.name: Check
nodes.summary: Public metadata-only preflight that an existing regular file may be edited under the policy; explicitly not race-safe authorization for a later write.

nodes.name: checkTarget
nodes.summary: Walks every path component without following links, requiring directory parents and a regular (or directory, for rename/delete) leaf, and applies store/name refusals.

nodes.name: refuse
nodes.summary: Fails when a target lies inside a configured store, has a protected name in any component, or (for directories) contains a store.

nodes.name: editHasParentComponent
nodes.summary: Reports whether a path contains a '..' component using native separators, before any cleaning.

nodes.name: editProtectedName
nodes.summary: Reports whether a path component is a protected credential or repository metadata name.

nodes.name: editResolveAncestor
nodes.summary: Resolves the longest existing ancestor of a path and appends missing components, rejecting dangling links, file parents and other failures.

nodes.name: edit_save.go
nodes.summary: Defines the save request/result contract for the text editor and the encoder that restores the original newline style and BOM from an LF editor snapshot.

nodes.name: SaveRequest
nodes.summary: Snapshot of an editor document to save; it does not authorize a write and has no force-write option.

nodes.name: SaveResult
nodes.summary: Either a saved baseline with new Content and revision, or a revision conflict carrying the observed revision.

nodes.name: encodeEditText
nodes.summary: Converts an LF editor snapshot back to the file's original newline style and BOM without adding or removing a final newline.

nodes.name: edit_target.go
nodes.summary: Opens an editable file through rooted handles, holding both the file and its original parent directory and verifying identities around a bounded raw-byte read.

nodes.name: Close
nodes.summary: Releases both the file and parent directory handles of an editTarget, even if one close fails.

nodes.name: sameDir
nodes.summary: Verifies that an opened directory handle is still the directory its path names.

nodes.name: openEditTargetFlag
nodes.summary: Repeats the edit preflight through rooted handles, opens the target read-only or read-write without creating it, and snapshots its bytes with identity checks.

nodes.name: edit_text.go
nodes.summary: Describes a text file's edit eligibility and format (newline style, BOM, revision hash) for the in-app editor.

nodes.name: EditInfo
nodes.summary: Edit eligibility, refusal reason and the newline/BOM format a save must keep for a text file.

nodes.name: textEditInfo
nodes.summary: Builds EditInfo for known-text data, detecting BOM, newline style and size limits.

nodes.name: newlineStyle
nodes.summary: Detects the single LF or CRLF line-ending style, reporting false for mixed endings or bare CR.

nodes.name: edit_write.go
nodes.summary: Implements edit eligibility completion and the in-place editor save: serialized saves, revision conflict detection, pre-write revalidation and write-then-truncate overwrite.
nodes.languageNotes: Rewrites files in place (like VS Code) to preserve identity, permissions and hard links, trading crash atomicity for metadata fidelity.

nodes.name: lockSaves
nodes.summary: Acquires the process-wide save slot or returns the context error, yielding a release function.

nodes.name: CheckEdit
nodes.summary: Completes a text read's edit eligibility by applying the policy and a writability check, updating only Eligible and Reason.

nodes.name: editReason
nodes.summary: Maps an edit-check error to a stable EditInfo refusal reason.

nodes.name: Save
nodes.summary: Saves an editor snapshot if the file still has the expected revision, returning a conflict otherwise; serializes saves via the save slot.

nodes.name: saveLocked
nodes.summary: Save body run with the save slot held: opens the target, compares revisions, encodes text, revalidates and overwrites.

nodes.name: revalidate
nodes.summary: Checks just before writing that the open file is still the snapshot's file, its path still names it and it still passes the policy.

nodes.name: overwrite
nodes.summary: Writes new bytes into the open file then truncates, wrapping every failure in ErrSaveIncomplete.

nodes.name: external.go
nodes.summary: Read-only viewer access to files outside any project (e.g. dependency sources a code definition points to), still refusing configured stores and protected names.

nodes.name: ReadExternal
nodes.summary: Reads an absolute external path for viewing only, checking both the given and resolved path against the policy with optional open store subdirectories.

nodes.name: opening
nodes.summary: Returns a policy with protected roots dropped when every target lies inside a resolved open directory.

nodes.name: files.go
nodes.summary: Core of the files package: lists project files (via git ls-files/status or a skip-aware walk with nested-repository handling), computes git status and line changes, and reads text or image contents for the file viewer.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of context-bound os/exec git invocations with -z NUL-framed output and an optional context-key callback for counting git calls in benchmarks.

nodes.name: Listing
nodes.summary: Sorted slash-separated project file listing with ignored files, ignored directories, git status and truncation flags.

nodes.name: LineChange
nodes.summary: A run of lines differing from the last commit, in current 1-based line numbers; deletions have Count 0.

nodes.name: Content
nodes.summary: One file read for display: text or base64 image, revision, edit info, line changes and size/binary flags.

nodes.name: List
nodes.summary: Lists files under root with git status, overlapping status collection with path enumeration.

nodes.name: ListPaths
nodes.summary: Enumerates project paths without collecting git status.

nodes.name: ListingStatus
nodes.summary: Collects git status for a listing independently of enumeration, querying nested repositories for walked listings.

nodes.name: listPaths
nodes.summary: Chooses git-based listing inside a work tree or a filesystem walk elsewhere, with callbacks for status overlap.

nodes.name: gitOutputEnv
nodes.summary: Runs the resolved git binary with timeout, hidden console, unquoted paths and extra environment.

nodes.name: gitFiles
nodes.summary: Lists tracked and untracked non-ignored files via git, expanding untracked nested worktrees.

nodes.name: gitIgnored
nodes.summary: Lists ignored files and folders up to a limit, adding files of ignored nested worktrees.

nodes.name: nestedRepositoryFiles
nodes.summary: Lists a nested worktree's own files relative to the outer root, using its own .gitignore.

nodes.name: gitStatus
nodes.summary: Returns per-path git status for changed files under root, or nil when git cannot tell.

nodes.name: parseStatus
nodes.summary: Parses git status --porcelain=v1 -z output into root-relative statuses.

nodes.name: statusOf
nodes.summary: Maps a porcelain XY status pair to the single letter VS Code would show.

nodes.name: parseHunks
nodes.summary: Parses a -U0 diff into LineChange runs from its hunk headers.

nodes.name: walk
nodes.summary: Filesystem walk entry point for roots outside any work tree.

nodes.name: walkPaths
nodes.summary: Walks a non-git root skipping dependency/build folders, listing nested repositories with their own ignore rules.

nodes.name: Resolve
nodes.summary: Resolves rel under root and refuses paths that escape root, including via symlinks.

nodes.name: Read
nodes.summary: Reads a file for display: text up to MaxReadBytes with edit info and line changes, or common images as base64.

nodes.name: readText
nodes.summary: Reads bounded text into Content, marking TooLarge or Binary when appropriate.

nodes.name: readImage
nodes.summary: Reads an image file as base64 unless it exceeds MaxImageBytes.

nodes.name: IsBinary
nodes.summary: Reports whether data contains a NUL byte or is not valid UTF-8.

nodes.name: git_branches.go
nodes.summary: Lists local and remote branches and switches the current branch, using the bounded git writer lock for consistent snapshots.

nodes.name: GitBranch
nodes.summary: A branch entry with name, remote flag and current marker.

nodes.name: GitBranchList
nodes.summary: Branch snapshot with the current branch and available branches.

nodes.name: GitSwitchRequest
nodes.summary: Request to switch to an existing or remote-tracking branch.

nodes.name: GitBranches
nodes.summary: Returns a consistent branch snapshot under the git write lock.

nodes.name: parseGitBranches
nodes.summary: Parses for-each-ref output into a GitBranchList.

nodes.name: GitSwitch
nodes.summary: Switches to a branch without forcing, validating the name and creating a tracking branch for remotes.

nodes.name: GitChangesRepository

nodes.name: ResolveGitChangesRepository

nodes.name: Paths
nodes.summary: Maps project-relative paths to repository paths, refusing any outside the repository.

nodes.name: Drafts
nodes.summary: Keeps only unsaved drafts inside the repository, as repository paths.

nodes.name: Path
nodes.summary: Maps a repository path back to a project-relative path.

nodes.name: Status
nodes.summary: Maps a RepoStatus's entries back to project-relative paths.

nodes.name: GitDiffContent
nodes.summary: Diff payload with original and modified Content and the basis used.

nodes.name: ReadGitDiff
nodes.summary: Reads one file's diff for a basis (working or staged), keeping index snapshots read-only and returning removal hunks for deleted entries.

nodes.name: readGitBlob
nodes.summary: Reads a bounded blob from the index or HEAD as display Content.

nodes.name: readGitWorking
nodes.summary: Reads the working-tree file as display Content, treating a missing file as empty.

nodes.name: git_history_actions.go
nodes.summary: Implements History panel ref actions (checkout, merge, delete, push and similar) with expected-OID checks, clean-state and protected-path preflights, and never forcing.

nodes.name: GitHistoryHeadIdentity
nodes.summary: Distinguishes attached branch, detached HEAD and unborn branch by OID and symbolic ref.

nodes.name: GitHistoryRefActionRequest
nodes.summary: Ref action request built from a confirmed snapshot, carrying the expected raw ref OID and head identity.

nodes.name: GitHistoryRefActionResult
nodes.summary: Result of a ref action with any message for the UI.

nodes.name: GitHistoryRefAction
nodes.summary: Performs a confirmed ref action after verifying the ref and HEAD still match the snapshot; never force-switches, force-pushes or force-deletes.

nodes.name: historyActionRef
nodes.summary: Resolves a ref's current raw object ID for the expected-OID check.

nodes.name: historyActionHead
nodes.summary: Reads the current HEAD identity (symbolic ref and OID, or unborn).

nodes.name: historyActionState
nodes.summary: Refuses actions while a merge/rebase is in progress or, when required, the tree is dirty.

nodes.name: historyActionPaths
nodes.summary: Refuses checkouts that would change paths protected by the edit policy.

nodes.name: historyActionCheckout

nodes.summary: Implements the CLI's `serve --stdio` subcommand, which runs the JSON-RPC 2.0 server that the desktop app talks to on WSL and SSH hosts, with nonce preface, idle timeout and engine startup during initialize.

nodes.name: serveCmd
nodes.summary: serveCmd runs the JSON-RPC server. resolveRoots runs during initialize, after the client's env overrides are applied, so the engine, its cache and the reported roots all use the overridden locations.

nodes.name: main.go
nodes.summary: Wails v3 desktop application entrypoint (behind the `desktop` build tag) that first dispatches to the Codex bridge, self-update helper and SSH askpass helper modes before launching the GUI.
nodes.languageNotes: Go build tags keep the GTK/WebKitGTK dependency out of plain `go build ./...` and `go test` runs; one binary multiplexes several helper roles by inspecting argv and environment.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Process entry point that dispatches to the Codex bridge, update-apply helper or askpass helper modes, raises the open-file limit, and otherwise runs the desktop app.

nodes.name: agent.go
nodes.summary: Scripted fake ACP agent used by tests: the test binary re-executes itself as the agent and each prompt's first word (stream, tool, permission, question, crash, ...) selects a scripted turn behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the Go TestMain self-exec pattern: the test binary doubles as the subprocess under test, selected via an environment variable.

nodes.name: agent
nodes.summary: State of the fake ACP agent: its connection, running turns, held turns, opened sessions, mode and behavior flags.

nodes.name: Main
nodes.summary: Main runs the fake agent, or its child, when the test binary was started as one, and exits.Otherwise it returns at once.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Command starts the fake agent in dir. env adds KEY=VALUE settings.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs the fake agent over stdio, optionally writing stderr filler, and waits until the connection ends (or forever when stubborn).

nodes.name: configOptions
nodes.summary: Returns the fake agent's session config options, such as its mode selector.

nodes.name: request
nodes.summary: Dispatches incoming ACP requests (initialize, session/new, load, resume, prompt, set_config_option, steering) and simulates adapter behaviors driven by environment flags.

nodes.name: steer
nodes.summary: Handles _session/steering: injects the message into a running turn as a 'steered:' chunk or answers promptRequired when idle.

nodes.name: notification
nodes.summary: Handles incoming notifications such as session/cancel by cancelling or releasing the matching turn.

nodes.name: prompt
nodes.summary: Executes one scripted prompt turn, choosing behavior from the first word (stream, tool, permission, hang, crash, flood, question, ...).

nodes.name: question
nodes.summary: Sends a form elicitation request using one of the QuestionForms and reports the client's answer back as a chunk.

nodes.name: describeBlocks
nodes.summary: describeBlocks lists a prompt's blocks, one per line: "text <text>", "image <mimeType> <bytes of base64>", "resource <uri> <mimeType> <text>", or the block's type.

nodes.name: client.go
nodes.summary: ACP client that starts an agent process, initializes the protocol and drives sessions (new/load/resume, prompt, steer, cancel, config options), answering permission and form-elicitation requests and shutting down the process tree gracefully.

nodes.name: Command
nodes.summary: Command is how to start an agent's ACP server.

nodes.name: ClientOptions
nodes.summary: ClientOptions configures a Client.Every field is optional.

nodes.name: Client
nodes.summary: Client drives one agent process over ACP.

nodes.name: ExitError
nodes.summary: ExitError is the error of a call whose agent went away.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Formats an ExitError with the method, exit status and the last line of the agent's stderr.

nodes.name: Unwrap
nodes.summary: Returns the underlying error of an ExitError for errors.Is/As.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Start starts the agent and initializes the connection. ctx bounds the start and the initialize call; the agent runs until Close.

nodes.name: Info
nodes.summary: Info is the agent's initialize reply.

nodes.name: Done
nodes.summary: Done is closed when the agent process has exited.

nodes.name: ExitErr
nodes.summary: ExitErr is the process's exit error once Done is closed; nil for status 0.When the connection broke first and the client killed the agent for it, it is the connection's error instead: ErrFrameTooLarge, ErrAgentGone or a read error.

nodes.name: StderrTail
nodes.summary: StderrTail is the end of the agent's stderr.

nodes.name: NewSession
nodes.summary: NewSession starts a session in cwd.

nodes.name: LoadSession
nodes.summary: LoadSession opens an existing session.The agent replays its history as updates before the call returns.

nodes.name: ResumeSession
nodes.summary: ResumeSession opens an existing session without replaying its history.

nodes.name: openSession
nodes.summary: Shared implementation of session/load and session/resume, rejecting methods the agent does not advertise.

nodes.name: SetConfigOption
nodes.summary: SetConfigOption changes a session option and returns the options as the agent now reports them.

nodes.name: Prompt
nodes.summary: Prompt runs one turn and returns its stop reason.Updates arrive through OnUpdate meanwhile.

nodes.name: CanSteer
nodes.summary: CanSteer reports whether the agent takes Steer.

nodes.name: Steer
nodes.summary: Steer adds prompt to the session's running turn (_session/steering).The outcome is SteerInjected, or SteerPromptRequired when no turn was running: the agent then started nothing, and the prompt is the caller's to send.

nodes.name: Cancel
nodes.summary: Cancel asks the agent to stop the session's turn and answers the session's pending permission requests Cancelled.

nodes.name: Close
nodes.summary: Close stops the agent and waits for it to exit.Pending permission requests are answered Cancelled first; then stdin is closed, then the tree is sent SIGTERM, then killed, each after the grace period.

nodes.name: waitExit
nodes.summary: Waits up to a duration for the agent process to exit and reports whether it did.

nodes.name: waitHandlers
nodes.summary: Waits up to a duration for in-flight request handlers to finish.

nodes.name: watch
nodes.summary: watch waits for the agent to exit, then stops what it left behind.

nodes.name: watchConn
nodes.summary: watchConn stops an agent whose connection ended under it.After an oversized message or a failed read nothing more is read from the agent, so it is killed and Done follows, rather than the chat looking live.

nodes.name: wrap
nodes.summary: wrap turns the error of a connection that ended under the client into an ExitError carrying the exit status and stderr.

nodes.name: handleNotification
nodes.summary: Forwards session/update notifications from the agent to the OnUpdate callback.

nodes.name: handleRequest
nodes.summary: handleRequest answers the agent.Permission requests and, with OnElicitation, forms are handled; without the fs and terminal capabilities, everything else is method-not-found.

nodes.name: wait
nodes.summary: wait registers a wait for the user on sessionID, which Cancel and Close end. ok is false when the client is closing.

nodes.name: askForm
nodes.summary: Validates a form elicitation request and asks the user through OnElicitation, answering cancelled when unsupported or when the wait ends.

nodes.name: askPermission
nodes.summary: Asks the user to answer an agent permission request through OnPermission, answering Cancelled when the session is cancelled or the client closes.

nodes.name: conn.go
nodes.summary: Bidirectional line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 connection to an agent, handling outgoing calls and notifications, incoming requests with cancellable handlers, $/cancel_request withdrawal and frame size limits.

nodes.name: ConnOptions
nodes.summary: ConnOptions configures a Conn.Every field is optional.

nodes.name: Conn
nodes.summary: Conn is a two-way JSON-RPC connection to an agent, one message per line.

nodes.name: NewConn
nodes.summary: NewConn starts reading r.Writes go to w; Close closes w when it is an io.Closer, which tells a stdio agent to exit.

nodes.name: Done
nodes.summary: Done is closed when the connection has ended.

nodes.name: Err
nodes.summary: Err is why the connection ended: ErrClosed, ErrAgentGone, ErrFrameTooLarge or a read error.It is nil while the connection is open.

nodes.name: Close
nodes.summary: Close ends the connection: pending calls fail with ErrClosed, handlers' contexts are cancelled, and w is closed.Messages still arriving are read and dropped until the agent closes its output.

nodes.name: finish
nodes.summary: finish ends the connection once, with the first reason given.

nodes.name: Call
nodes.summary: Call sends a request and decodes its result into result, which may be nil.It returns the agent's *Error, the connection's error, or ctx's error.

nodes.name: call
nodes.summary: Sends a JSON-RPC request, registers its pending reply and waits for the result, connection end or context cancellation, optionally withdrawing it.

nodes.name: CallWithdrawing
nodes.summary: CallWithdrawing is Call, but when ctx ends first it also tells the other side to drop the request with $/cancel_request, and its late reply is not reported as a protocol error.

nodes.name: Notify
nodes.summary: Notify sends a notification.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Encodes and writes one JSON-RPC message as a line, serialized under the write lock.

nodes.name: readLoop
nodes.summary: Reads line-delimited messages until EOF or error, dispatching each and ending the connection with the reason.

nodes.name: dispatch
nodes.summary: Parses one incoming line and routes it as a reply, request, notification or $/cancel_request.

nodes.name: handleReply
nodes.summary: Delivers a reply to its pending call, reporting unknown reply IDs as protocol errors.

nodes.name: withdraw
nodes.summary: withdraw cancels the request a $/cancel_request names.

nodes.name: handleRequest
nodes.summary: Runs the request handler for an incoming request in its own cancellable context and writes the result or error reply.

nodes.name: readLine
nodes.summary: readLine reads one line of at most limit bytes, without its newline and surrounding space.A longer line returns ErrFrameTooLarge.

nodes.name: elicitation.go
nodes.summary: Types and validation for ACP form elicitation (elicitation/create), the mechanism agents use to ask the user questions; keeps field order, checks support for the schema and validates submitted answers.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom UnmarshalJSON/MarshalJSON preserve JSON object key order, which Go maps would otherwise lose.

nodes.name: ElicitationCapabilities
nodes.summary: ElicitationCapabilities says which elicitation modes the client shows.A present Form means form mode.

nodes.name: CancelRequestNotification
nodes.summary: CancelRequestNotification is the params of $/cancel_request.

nodes.name: CreateElicitationRequest
nodes.summary: CreateElicitationRequest is the params of elicitation/create.Only session-scoped form mode is shown; RequestID scopes a request outside a session, such as a login.

nodes.name: CreateElicitationResponse
nodes.summary: CreateElicitationResponse answers elicitation/create.

nodes.name: ElicitationSchema
nodes.summary: ElicitationSchema is a form: an object of flat properties.

nodes.name: ElicitationField
nodes.summary: ElicitationField is one named property.

nodes.name: ElicitationProperty
nodes.summary: ElicitationProperty is one field of a form.Unknown names a key this client does not know, which makes the field unsupported.

nodes.name: ElicitationItems
nodes.summary: ElicitationItems are a multi-select's options.

nodes.name: EnumOption
nodes.summary: EnumOption is a titled option.

nodes.name: ElicitationCancelled
nodes.summary: ElicitationCancelled is the answer to a form the user never answered: the turn was cancelled, the chat closed or the agent withdrew it.

nodes.name: UnmarshalJSON
nodes.summary: UnmarshalJSON keeps the properties in the order they were sent.

nodes.name: MarshalJSON
nodes.summary: MarshalJSON writes the properties as an object, in order.

nodes.name: Field
nodes.summary: Field returns the property named key.

nodes.name: Supported
nodes.summary: Supported reports why a form cannot be shown in full, or nil when it can.

nodes.name: supported
nodes.summary: Reports why a single elicitation property cannot be shown, based on its type, format and options.

nodes.name: checkOptions
nodes.summary: Rejects enum option lists that are empty or contain duplicate values.

nodes.name: options
nodes.summary: options are a choice's or a multi-select's options, titled.

nodes.name: Validate
nodes.summary: Validate checks an accepted form's content against the schema and returns it with each value in its JSON type.A key the form does not have, a missing required field or a value out of bounds is an error.

nodes.name: ValidateValues
nodes.summary: ValidateValues is Validate for content already decoded from JSON, or built in Go.

nodes.name: value
nodes.summary: Decodes and validates one submitted field value against the property's type, enum options and bounds.

nodes.name: tail.go
nodes.summary: Small ring-style buffer that keeps the last bytes of an agent's stderr for inclusion in error reports.

nodes.name: tailBuffer
nodes.summary: tailBuffer keeps the last max bytes written to it: the end of an agent's stderr, for error reports.

nodes.name: Write
nodes.summary: Appends bytes to the tail buffer, discarding the oldest data beyond its capacity.

nodes.name: String
nodes.summary: String returns the kept bytes.When older output was dropped, it starts at the first whole line.

nodes.name: types.go
nodes.summary: Package acp's protocol types for the ACP v1 subset used by chat mode: JSON-RPC errors, initialize/session/prompt/steer requests, content blocks, session updates with typed decoders, and permission requests.
nodes.languageNotes: SessionUpdate keeps its raw JSON alongside the kind so unknown update kinds and _meta extensions round-trip untouched.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Error is a JSON-RPC error, sent or received.

nodes.name: Implementation
nodes.summary: Implementation names a client or an agent.

nodes.name: ClientCapabilities
nodes.summary: ClientCapabilities leaves out fs and terminal on purpose: without them the agent must not call the client's file or terminal methods.Elicitation is set only when the client shows forms.

nodes.name: InitializeRequest
nodes.summary: Params of the ACP initialize call: protocol version, client capabilities and client info.

nodes.name: InitializeResponse
nodes.summary: Agent's initialize reply with protocol version, capabilities, auth methods and agent info.

nodes.name: AgentCapabilities
nodes.summary: Capabilities an agent advertises, including session load/resume and prompt content support.

nodes.name: PromptCapabilities
nodes.summary: Which prompt content an agent accepts: images, audio and embedded context.

nodes.name: AuthMethod
nodes.summary: AuthMethod is a way to log in, such as "Run `opencode auth login` in the terminal".

nodes.name: NewSessionRequest
nodes.summary: Params of session/new: working directory and MCP servers.

nodes.name: SessionSetup
nodes.summary: SessionSetup is what session/new, session/load and session/resume return.

nodes.name: LoadSessionRequest
nodes.summary: LoadSessionRequest is the params of session/load and of session/resume.

nodes.name: ConfigOption
nodes.summary: ConfigOption is one session setting such as mode, model or effort.

nodes.name: ConfigSelectOption
nodes.summary: ConfigSelectOption is a value of a select option, or a named group of values when Group is set.

nodes.name: SetConfigOptionRequest
nodes.summary: Params of session/set_config_option naming the session, option and new value.

nodes.name: SetConfigOptionResponse
nodes.summary: Reply to set_config_option carrying the session's updated config options.

nodes.name: ContentBlock
nodes.summary: ContentBlock is a prompt or message part.Type is text, image, audio, resource_link or resource.

nodes.name: TextResource
nodes.summary: TextResource is the text of an embedded resource.

nodes.name: PromptRequest
nodes.summary: Params of session/prompt: session ID and the prompt's content blocks.

nodes.name: SteerRequest
nodes.summary: Params of _session/steering adding a prompt to a session's running turn.

nodes.name: SteerMeta
nodes.summary: _meta wrapper carrying steering options on a steer request.

nodes.name: SteerOptions
nodes.summary: Steering options such as idleBehavior.

nodes.name: SteerResponse
nodes.summary: Reply to a steer request reporting whether the prompt was injected or a prompt is required.

nodes.name: PromptResponse
nodes.summary: Reply to session/prompt carrying the turn's stop reason.

nodes.name: CancelNotification
nodes.summary: Params of session/cancel naming the session whose turn to stop.

nodes.name: SessionNotification
nodes.summary: SessionNotification is the params of session/update.

nodes.name: SessionUpdate
nodes.summary: SessionUpdate keeps the update's raw JSON next to its kind, so unknown kinds and extension fields survive.The As* methods decode known kinds.

nodes.name: ContentChunk
nodes.summary: ContentChunk is a user_message_chunk, agent_message_chunk or agent_thought_chunk.

nodes.name: ToolCall
nodes.summary: ToolCall is a tool_call, or a tool_call_update in which every field but ToolCallID may be absent (nil).

nodes.name: ToolCallContent
nodes.summary: ToolCallContent is one of: content (a block), diff, or terminal.

nodes.name: ToolLocation
nodes.summary: File path and optional line a tool call touches.

nodes.name: PlanEntry
nodes.summary: One entry of an agent plan with content, priority and status.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.summary: A plan update listing the agent's current plan entries.

nodes.name: ConfigOptionUpdate
nodes.summary: A config_option_update carrying the session's current config options.

nodes.name: CurrentModeUpdate
nodes.summary: A current_mode_update naming the session's new mode.

nodes.name: PermissionOption
nodes.summary: One choice offered in a permission request, with ID, name and kind (allow/reject, once/always).

nodes.name: RequestPermissionRequest
nodes.summary: RequestPermissionRequest is the params of session/request_permission.

nodes.name: PermissionOutcome
nodes.summary: Outcome of a permission request: selected with an option ID, or cancelled.

nodes.name: RequestPermissionResponse
nodes.summary: Client's reply to session/request_permission wrapping the outcome.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Formats the JSON-RPC error as a string with its code and message.

nodes.name: Reason
nodes.summary: Reason is data.reason, which some adapters set to say why they refused a request (codex-acp: "thread_active_writer"), or "" without one.

nodes.name: IsSessionInUse
nodes.summary: IsSessionInUse reports whether err is the agent refusing a session that another of its own processes has open.

nodes.name: MethodNotFound
nodes.summary: MethodNotFound is the reply to a request the client does not handle.

nodes.name: IsAuthRequired
nodes.summary: IsAuthRequired reports whether err is the agent saying it needs a login.

nodes.name: CanSteer
nodes.summary: CanSteer reports whether the agent advertises _session/steering (_meta.steering.supported).

nodes.name: CanResume
nodes.summary: CanResume reports whether the agent advertises session/resume.

nodes.name: mcpServers.MarshalJSON
nodes.summary: Marshals the MCP server list, always emitting [] instead of null.

nodes.name: TextBlock
nodes.summary: TextBlock is a text content block.

nodes.name: ImageBlock
nodes.summary: ImageBlock is an image content block; data is the image in base64.Only for agents that advertise promptCapabilities.image.

nodes.name: ResourceBlock
nodes.summary: ResourceBlock embeds a text resource in a prompt.Only for agents that advertise promptCapabilities.embeddedContext.

nodes.name: UnmarshalJSON
nodes.summary: Decodes a session update, keeping its raw JSON and extracting the sessionUpdate kind.

nodes.name: SessionUpdate.MarshalJSON
nodes.summary: Re-emits a session update's preserved raw JSON.

nodes.name: AsChunk
nodes.summary: AsChunk decodes a message or thought chunk.

nodes.name: AsToolCall
nodes.summary: AsToolCall decodes a tool_call or tool_call_update.

nodes.name: AsPlan
nodes.summary: AsPlan decodes a plan update, which replaces the previous plan.

nodes.name: AsConfigOptions
nodes.summary: AsConfigOptions decodes a config_option_update.

nodes.name: AsCurrentMode
nodes.summary: AsCurrentMode decodes a current_mode_update.

nodes.name: Option
nodes.summary: Option returns the option with the given ID.

nodes.name: Selected
nodes.summary: Selected answers a permission request with one of its options.

nodes.name: Cancelled
nodes.summary: Cancelled answers a permission request whose turn was cancelled.

nodes.summary: Thin package-local wrappers delegating resume-command formatting and shell escaping to the engine package.

nodes.summary: Wails-bound App methods to read and update which agents are enabled, delegating to the active backend.

nodes.name: GetAgentSettings

nodes.name: SetAgentSettings
nodes.summary: Updates the enabled agents on the active backend and returns the new settings.

nodes.name: localChatService

nodes.name: remoteChats

nodes.summary: Adapts the local engine chat manager's Agents to the chatService interface.

nodes.name: localChatService.ChatStart
nodes.summary: Adapts the local engine chat manager's Start to the chatService interface.

nodes.name: localChatService.ChatPrompt
nodes.summary: Adapts the local engine chat manager's Prompt to the chatService interface.

nodes.summary: Adapts the local engine chat manager's Cancel to the chatService interface.

nodes.summary: Adapts the local engine chat manager's List to the chatService interface.

nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatAgents and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.name: remoteChats.ChatStart
nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatStart and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.name: remoteChats.ChatPrompt
nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatPrompt and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.name: remoteChats.ChatSendNow
nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatSendNow and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.name: remoteChats.ChatUnqueue
nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatUnqueue and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatCancel and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatAnswer and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.summary: Calls the remote host's ChatSetOption and maps a missing chat capability to ErrChatRemote.

nodes.name: App.ChatAgents
nodes.summary: ChatAgents reports, for each agent that can run in a chat, whether its ACP adapter is installed on the host the window shows and how to install it.

nodes.name: App.ChatStart
nodes.summary: ChatStart starts the agent's ACP adapter in req.Dir: a new session, or the session req.Resume names.Updates arrive as chat:update events and the end as chat:exit.

nodes.name: App.ChatPrompt
nodes.summary: ChatPrompt sends text and attachments to the chat's agent.It returns once the turn has started; the turn's end arrives as a turn_end update.

nodes.name: App.ChatSendNow
nodes.summary: ChatSendNow sends a queued message at once: it starts a turn when the agent is idle, or joins the running turn when the agent steers.

nodes.name: App.ChatUnqueue
nodes.summary: ChatUnqueue removes a queued message and returns it with its attachments, for the composer to edit.

nodes.name: App.ChatCancel
nodes.summary: ChatCancel cancels the chat's running turn and answers its pending permission requests cancelled.

nodes.name: App.ChatRespond
nodes.summary: ChatRespond answers a permission request with one of its options, or cancelled when optionID is empty.

nodes.name: App.ChatAnswer
nodes.summary: ChatAnswer answers one of the agent's questions (a question update): action is accept, with content checked against the question's form, or decline (the user skipped it) or cancel.

nodes.name: App.ChatSetOption
nodes.summary: ChatSetOption sets one of the session's options (mode, model, effort) and returns them all as the agent reports them.

nodes.name: App.ChatClose
nodes.summary: ChatClose ends the chat and its agent.Pending permission requests are answered cancelled.

nodes.name: App.ChatList
nodes.summary: ChatList returns the window's open chats, so a reloaded frontend can find them again.

nodes.summary: SetChatsOpen tells the window's close guard whether the window has an open chat.A host's chats run on the host, which the guard cannot ask without waiting; the frontend knows them.

nodes.name: windowBusy
nodes.summary: windowBusy reports whether closing the window would end something that runs: a terminal or a chat.The close guard calls it on the UI thread, so it never waits.

nodes.name: desktop.go
nodes.summary: Defines the Desktop adapter the GUI shell injects (dialogs, events, window control, notifications) and the lifecycle entry points OnStartup, OnBeforeClose, OnShutdown and Close, keeping the app package toolkit-free.

nodes.name: FileFilter
nodes.summary: FileFilter is one entry of a native file dialog's type list.Pattern holds semicolon-separated globs such as "*.agent-session.zip;*.zip".

nodes.name: OpenDialogOptions
nodes.summary: OpenDialogOptions describes a native picker for files or a directory.

nodes.name: SaveDialogOptions
nodes.summary: SaveDialogOptions describes a native save dialog.

nodes.name: MessageDialogOptions
nodes.summary: MessageDialogOptions describes a native message dialog.

nodes.name: Desktop
nodes.summary: Desktop is everything this package needs from the desktop shell.The shell builds it from its GUI toolkit and passes it to OnStartup; this package never imports the toolkit, so default builds stay GUI-free.

nodes.name: Emit
nodes.summary: Forwards an engine event to the injected desktop emit callback, if any.

nodes.name: OnStartup
nodes.summary: OnStartup starts the local engine and desktop event routing.The shell calls it once, before the frontend makes any binding call.

nodes.name: OnBeforeClose

nodes.name: OnShutdown

nodes.name: Close
nodes.summary: Close stops background scans, watchers, indexers and the database without touching desktop notifications.Non-desktop callers use it instead of OnShutdown.

nodes.name: DiscoveryStatusReply

nodes.name: DiscoveryStatusEvent
nodes.summary: DiscoveryStatusEvent is the Wails payload of engine.DiscoveryStatusEvent: the engine snapshot plus the route it came from.Host is empty for Local.

nodes.name: DiscoveryStatus
nodes.summary: DiscoveryStatus reports the active backend's startup discovery status.An offline host keeps its disconnected error.

nodes.name: export.go

nodes.name: PreviewExport

nodes.summary: PortForwardRequest is a saved rule.Empty ID creates a new rule; otherwise SavePortForward updates the rule on the currently selected SSH host.

nodes.name: PortForwardRule
nodes.summary: A saved forward rule with its live status and error, as shown in the UI.

nodes.name: PortForwardSnapshot
nodes.summary: Snapshot of the selected host's port-forward rules and any load error.

nodes.summary: portForwards holds the saved rules and this process's running forwards.Several app windows (processes) share the rules file: each reads it again before use, and changes it under the config lock from its current contents, so one window's edits never overwrite another's.

nodes.name: forwardLog
nodes.summary: forwardLog bounds diagnostics and recognizes OpenSSH's post-authentication readiness marker, rather than assuming a successfully spawned process works.

nodes.summary: loadLocked reads the rules file again, picking up changes made by other windows.A file that cannot be read keeps the last rules and sets loadErr, which blocks writes so they never overwrite rules this window did not see.

nodes.name: updateLocked
nodes.summary: updateLocked changes the rules file under the config lock: it reads the file as it is now, lets edit change a copy of every host's rules and writes the result.

nodes.name: sync
nodes.summary: sync is called with connection.mu held, serializing lifecycle changes with API operations.It never waits for an SSH process to authenticate or exit.

nodes.name: snapshotLocked
nodes.summary: Builds the snapshot of the current host's rules and run states; caller holds the lock.

nodes.name: persistLocked
nodes.summary: Writes all hosts' saved rules to the rules file atomically; caller holds the lock.

nodes.name: startLocked
nodes.summary: Starts an ssh process for a rule in the background, tracking its starting/active/failed status through forwardLog.

nodes.name: Write
nodes.summary: Captures ssh output, bounding diagnostics and marking the forward ready when OpenSSH reports authentication succeeded.

nodes.name: withForwards

nodes.summary: Stops a running port-forward rule.

nodes.summary: Stops and deletes a saved port-forward rule.

nodes.summary: Returns a copy of the host environment overrides passed to remote servers.

nodes.summary: Connect begins a connection to alias.Coming from Local, Local stays the active backend until the remote handshake finishes; coming from another host, calls fail as disconnected meanwhile.

nodes.summary: Dials the remote serve session with backoff, publishing disconnected/reconnecting/connected phases, and stays generation-safe against newer connects.

nodes.name: permanentDialError

nodes.summary: Disconnect returns to Local and stops reconnects.The selected host is cleared.

nodes.summary: releaseHost closes the ssh master for alias after its session is closed.A missing master (never started, or already gone) is not an error worth reporting.

nodes.name: closeLocked
nodes.summary: Closes the current remote session and transport; caller holds the lock.

nodes.name: codex-rollout-repair.md

nodes.name: formats.md

Also records the M6-02 spike results for export, import, and restore workflows across all three providers.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents three distinct storage paradigms (JSONL transcripts, SQLite WAL databases, rollout envelopes) that the provider parsers must all handle defensively against format drift.

nodes.name: perf.md
nodes.summary: Cumulative performance and QA evidence log for the project, opening with the M1 MVP QA pass against the SPEC section 8 targets (scan, transcript load, scroll FPS, binary size, memory) and then recording dated task entries PF/ST/IT/PI/NG/PC with methods, before/after measurements, verification commands, and explicit limits. Each milestone (1: scan and load baselines, 2: incremental transcripts, 3: project listings) closes with an integrated gate entry stating what passed and what remains unperformed.
nodes.languageNotes: Entries follow a strict evidence discipline: every claim names its workload, host, and limits, and unperformed checks (native GUI, SSH, WSL, Windows) are explicitly excluded rather than waived.

nodes.name: M0.md
nodes.summary: Detailed M0 plan defining the shared contracts every later milestone builds on (module layout, model types, provider.Provider interface, JSONL reader, path utils) plus the read-only Claude Code provider and the headless CLI, as tasks M0-01 through M0-16 with cross-milestone conventions.
nodes.languageNotes: Task breakdown uses hour estimates and explicit contract sections that later plans cite as authoritative.

nodes.name: M1-gui
nodes.summary: Detailed plan for the desktop GUI (tasks M1-15 through M1-28): a Wails shell with strict boundary isolation, a Svelte 5 frontend that talks only through lib/api.ts with a mock backend, virtualized session list and transcript viewer, syntax highlighting, progressive loading, WebView hardening and an MVP QA pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Describes Wails v2; the repo has since moved to Wails v3 (see the wails-v3-upgrade feature plan).

nodes.name: M1-providers.md
nodes.summary: Detailed plan for the OpenCode and Codex providers and the scan/group core (tasks M1-01 through M1-14): read-only SQLite and rollout parsing across storage generations, message counts and resume, a concurrent scan orchestrator with in-memory catalog, and a pure grouping engine, all strictly read-only over tool stores.
nodes.languageNotes: Records measured local observations (DB sizes, query timings) to justify fast-path choices.

nodes.name: M2.md
nodes.summary: Detailed plan for indexing, search and live updates (tasks M2-01 through M2-12): a private SQLite cache with migrations and cache-first startup, incremental scans, background FTS5 indexing, a ranked search API with jump-to-message UI, fsnotify watchers, Wails events, live transcript tail and a diagnostics panel.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines transactional invariants (scan state and cache commit atomically per provider) that later plans rely on.

nodes.name: M3-M5.md
nodes.summary: Combined detailed plan for M3 polish (filters, config, exports, keyboard navigation, stats), M4 opt-in destructive actions (Linux Trash transport, per-agent delete/manage behind HMAC-previewed tokens) and M5 distribution (macOS port, signing/notarization, Linux packaging, CI tagged releases).
nodes.languageNotes: M4 stays optional behind opt-in with a preview/confirm HMAC token flow shared with M6 restore.

nodes.name: M6.md
nodes.summary: Plan for portable sessions and cross-agent handoff (tasks M6-01 through M6-17): a versioned zip bundle (manifest v1) carrying verbatim native records for same-agent restore and a budgeted, redacted Markdown handoff document for continuing a session in a different agent, with HMAC-guarded restore and CLI support.
nodes.languageNotes: Explains why restore copies raw native records instead of the clipped model.Transcript display model.

nodes.name: M7.md
nodes.summary: Architecture plan for remote sessions over SSH (tasks M7-01 through M7-21): a Wails-free engine shared by a headless agent-sessions-cli serve --stdio server on the remote, JSON-RPC over ssh stdio with askpass dialogs, auto-deployed server builds, artifact transfer, connection semantics and multi-process index sharing rules.
nodes.languageNotes: Specifies transport hardening (nonce preface, frame caps, $/ping liveness) and a writer/reader lock protocol for the shared index cache.

nodes.name: M8.md

nodes.languageNotes: Anchored in a real GOOS=windows cross-compile check and Codex launcher research with upstream source links.

nodes.name: README.md

nodes.name: idle-rendering-qa.md
nodes.summary: QA and measurement record for the idle-rendering plan: Metal trace evidence of macOS GPU load from compositor-driven animation, iterative fixes (IR-02 through IR-07) including shared discrete indicator clocks and a native NSWindow opacity experiment, user-reported GPU results down to 0% idle, and the native validation gates still open on all three platforms.

nodes.name: idle-rendering.md
nodes.summary: Plan to reduce idle animation and compositing cost across desktop platforms: static liveness badges, IntersectionObserver-gated spinners and dots driven by shared discrete timers, and an approved native macOS window-opacity experiment to cut WindowServer compositing, without pausing animations globally or touching terminal behavior.

nodes.name: layout-memory.md
nodes.summary: Plan for content-fit window and pane sizing with memory: first-run size computed from the screen, transcript header width measured with canvas measureText, remembered user layout winning over calculated layout, and Go-side window geometry persistence (window-state.json) with maximised-flag handling and work-area clamping.

nodes.name: linux-gpu-rendering.md
nodes.summary: Plan to restore WebKit's DMA-BUF GPU renderer on Linux by removing the app's WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 init override and trusting Wails v3's NVIDIA-only detection, ending software compositing that pinned the GTK main thread at 100% on fractional scales.

nodes.name: linux-repos-keys.md
nodes.summary: Operations runbook for the two Ed25519 OpenPGP signing keys behind the apt/dnf repositories: key creation with repo-keys.sh, encrypted backups, secret storage in Cloudflare Workers and GitHub environments, dated renewal and rotation procedures, leak response, and the LR-15 cross-distro apt/rpm verification matrix that the procedure is based on.

nodes.name: linux-repos.md
nodes.summary: Plan for apt and dnf package repositories so Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora users get every stable release via upgrade: packages stay on GitHub Releases while a Cloudflare Worker with Postgres/Hyperdrive serves signed index generations, RPMs are signed in release CI with a separate key, and every stable release stays listed to avoid stale-index 404s.

nodes.name: macos-terminal-input-qa.md
nodes.summary: Investigation evidence for macOS terminal Vietnamese input: narrows the failure to plain remote shells starting in POSIX/ASCII locale (readline garbling IME replacement text), shows the remote-locale diagnostics, and records the MTI-03 fix that exports an installed UTF-8 LANG when all locale variables are unset.

nodes.name: macos-terminal-input.md
nodes.summary: Plan to accept Vietnamese replacement text from OpenKey, EVKey and GoTiengViet in the embedded terminal: investigate native WebKit keyboard events and xterm input routing before changing handling, and add a remote plain-shell bootstrap that discovers a UTF-8 locale only when LANG, LC_CTYPE and LC_ALL are all unset.

nodes.name: manual-bash-transcript.md
nodes.summary: Plan to render Claude Code's user-run ! Bash commands as compact terminal-style command/output cards instead of chat bubbles containing bash-input/bash-stdout wrappers, keeping generated titles and previews free of wrapper and output noise.

nodes.name: message-file-single-match.md
nodes.summary: Plan to open a recovered message/terminal file path directly when the project search finds exactly one match, keeping the chooser toast for several matches and for single matches from truncated listings, with re-resolution and authorization unchanged.

nodes.name: nested-repo-blame.md
nodes.summary: Bug analysis showing line blame never appears in nested repositories below a non-Git root: the viewer gates blame on the listing's git flag even though files.BlameFile already discovers Git per file, so only the gate is wrong.

nodes.name: nested-repo-gitignore.md
nodes.summary: Plan to honor per-repository Git ignore rules when listing a non-Git project root: the tree walk asks each nested repository's Git once (budgeted ls-files queries), sorts entries into Files/Ignored/IgnoredDirectories, and keeps the blame bar with an 'Ignored by Git' message instead of closing it.

nodes.name: orphan-task-notifications.md
nodes.summary: Plan to present Claude Code's orphaned-background-task <task-notification> envelope as a proper assistant notification instead of raw XML in a user bubble, with repeated task-id parsing, marker-ID filtering and fallback to raw text for unknown fields.

nodes.name: performance-m2.md
nodes.summary: Design for Performance Milestone 2, incremental transcripts: resumable provider loads with split-point equivalence to cold loads, a copy-on-write message store, stat-only Codex rollout resolution, a byte-bounded transcript cache, shared FTS loading, and a delta wire API so appends cost only the appended bytes.

nodes.name: performance-m3.md
nodes.summary: Design for Performance Milestone 3, a shared per-root project index: split path enumeration from Git status, coalesce concurrent listing flights with generation-based invalidation, retain explicitly unverified path snapshots with bounded memory, and always reconcile on authoritative requests instead of trusting watchers.

nodes.name: performance-startup.md
nodes.summary: Design and evidence log for the startup-responsiveness package (ST-00 through ST-08): engine-owned readiness/status snapshots with honest terminal outcomes, a compatibility policy for older hosts, truthful empty/discovering frontend states, large-index integrity measurement follow-ups, and a remote early-catalog handshake under RPC Serve.

nodes.name: performance.md
nodes.summary: Performance improvement roadmap across five milestones (baselines and coalescing, startup slice, incremental transcripts, shared project index, catalog scaling and rendering), with delivery status per milestone, shared guardrails around fixtures and authorization, and a verification policy of barrier-based concurrency tests and measured distributions.

nodes.name: print-page-setup.md
nodes.summary: Plan for cross-platform print page setup in the print editor: A4/Letter, portrait/landscape and uniform margin controls carried on PrintDocument as a generated @page rule, with per-platform native adapters (WebKitPrintOperation on Linux, WKWebView bridge on macOS, WebView2 window.print on Windows).

nodes.name: remote-reconnect-qa.md
nodes.summary: Measurement record for remote reconnection: before/after Docker sshd fault-injection timings showing detection drop from ~59 s to 21 s against 25 s/15 s bounds, the RR-08 inherited-stderr-pipe fix found by the first failed run, verification suite results, and an explicit table of unperformed native Windows/WSL/macOS checks.

nodes.name: remote-reconnect.md
nodes.summary: Plan for fast recovery from interrupted remote connections: an RPC byte-level liveness watchdog with $/ping (20 s deadline), ControlMaster teardown after silent drops, a 45 s limit on automatic probe attempts, a flatter backoff, always-visible Retry, and same-host reconnects that keep the selected session and history.

nodes.name: review-fixes.md
nodes.summary: Plan to fix the findings of the 2026-11-14 architecture and feature review: release-environment and supply-chain hardening (RF-01 to RF-03, RF-08), untrusted-content execution and privacy gaps (RF-04 to RF-10), a table of 18 reliability bugs with per-task check status (RF-11 to RF-28), and CI/docs gaps, plus unimplemented architecture proposals.

nodes.name: selection-translate.md
nodes.summary: Plan for a selected-text context menu in transcript messages with Copy and Translate-to-{language}: bounded surrounding sentences go to the model as context, only the selection is translated into a transient popover, and cross-message or header selections keep the native menu.

nodes.name: session-mono-font.md
nodes.summary: Plan (implemented) for a Settings checkbox that applies the editor's monospace font to session content via a --font-mono override scoped to the transcript pane, with regression tests that forbid hardcoded font-family and browser-default monospace in session parts.

nodes.name: session-scrollbar.md
nodes.summary: Plan and experiment log for Linux session-list scrollbar stability: seven failed candidates before a one-line translateZ(0) compositing layer on the virtual list's scroll container fixed the missing/flashing WebKitGTK scrollbar, followed by SS-08 to SS-10 per-surface layers that stopped header, Resume/New and navigation/badge flicker.

nodes.name: swipe-navigation-windows-linux.md
nodes.summary: Plan to bring two-finger swipe back/forward to Windows and Linux: a GtkEventControllerScroll gesture detector on Linux and Raw Input Precision Touchpad contact parsing on Windows (after the wheel-event heuristic failed under load), with SwipeGuard keeping sideways-scrolling gestures as scrolls and text fields counted as scrollable.

nodes.name: swipe-navigation.md
nodes.summary: Plan for macOS two-finger swipe back/forward like Safari: the native NSEvent monitor spots the swipe from phased scroll events (80 pt, 2:1 horizontal ratio, gated on the system's Swipe-between-pages setting) and the frontend SwipeGuard drops it while the gesture could still scroll something sideways.

nodes.name: switch-to-chat.md
nodes.summary: Plan to move a session from a terminal tab to a live chat in one click: a tab-menu item with attention-state-aware confirmation wording, coordinated by ChatOpener.switchToChat which closes only the session's pane and resumes the saved session in a new chat with focused composer.

nodes.name: terminal-auto-activation.md
nodes.summary: Plan for a default-enabled Settings preference that gates automatic terminal-tab activation when selecting or focusing sessions, routed through the shared terminal-selection entry point so browsing never interrupts the chosen shell or agent tab when disabled.

nodes.name: terminal-cwd-matching.md
nodes.summary: Plan so a manually selected shell keeps matching a session's workspace via its reported cwd (tab.cwd || tab.dir) even when it reached the workspace with cd, leaving agent-pane matching, ranking and focus guards unchanged.

nodes.name: terminal-file-paths.md
nodes.summary: Plan so Ctrl/Cmd-click on terminal tool output like Update(docs/.../README.md) opens the inner path: structural tool-call wrapper detection with exact UTF-16 offsets for the xterm provider, quoted arguments and line/column suffixes supported, filename parentheses preserved.

nodes.name: terminal-maximize.md
nodes.summary: Stub plan for internal terminal maximization, dated 2026-10-24, containing only a link to its terminal-maximize task group; the design lives in the task briefs.

nodes.name: terminal-split.md
nodes.summary: Plan for split terminals: a tab becomes a group of one to four panes where each pane is one PTY, terminals.tabs stays the flat pane list so session links, attention and closing keep working on pane ids, and pane groups own the tab strip without persistence.

nodes.name: tool-file-links.md
nodes.summary: Plan to make file paths in tool-card headers clickable: toolFileTarget extracts file_path/filePath/notebook_path (and path on file tools) from tool input with Read offset line support, opening through the same authorized viewer path as message file links.

nodes.name: tool-installation.md
nodes.summary: Design and evidence log for consent-based managed language-server installation (TI-01 to TI-04): a closed gopls/Ruff/vtsls catalog built with a reviewed trusted Go toolchain under an allowlisted environment, one-shot consent tokens, atomic private staging and receipt-validated publication, Engine ownership and cancellation, an optional App/managedTool RPC contract with bounded job polling, and frontend Install/Not-now setup controls.

nodes.name: transcript-directory-links.md
nodes.summary: Plan to stop offering file-opening actions for transcript paths ending in a directory separator: the shared file-destination parser rejects trailing / or \ after URI decoding and suffix removal, while valid file paths and source locations stay unchanged.

nodes.name: transcript-page-cap.md
nodes.summary: Plan to cap transcript pages by size as well as count: a server-side PageCap with an anchor message grows the page outward within a 256 KB budget so Codex first pages shrink from up to 1.29 MB, wired through GetMessagesCapped over RPC/Wails with wire-compatible fallbacks and viewer anchor handling for all four request kinds.

nodes.name: transcript-tool-readability.md
nodes.summary: Plan to make Activity/All tool cards scannable: command/path summaries instead of opaque call IDs, decoded JSON text-content envelopes with verbatim fallback, collapsible long outputs with search-aware expansion, and comfortable typography that follows the session font scale.

nodes.name: wails-v3-upgrade.md
nodes.summary: State-of-record for the Wails v2 to v3 migration (v3.1.0, GTK4/WebKitGTK 6 on Linux): code boundaries (single Router.Call binding, dynamic @wailsio/runtime import, per-window App instances), platform packaging, what CI and the user verified, and an explicit checklist of native manual gates not yet run.

nodes.name: windows-ci-test-stability.md
nodes.summary: Plan to remove two timing assumptions behind windows-test-build failures: a generous deadline isolating the Git call-cap test from Windows process startup, and a barrier-based fake-watcher readiness signal after initial publication instead of sleeps, with production limits unchanged.

nodes.name: workspace-filter-release.md
nodes.summary: Plan to release the sidebar workspace filter: clicking the group tree's empty space (or Escape) clears the group filter as a navigation step Back can undo, keeping the open session, and a quieter 'current' highlight distinguishes the open session's group from the filtering row.

nodes.name: SN-02.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-02: Windows swipe detection from page wheel events in SwipeGuard (gesture grouping, mouse/Shift/line-mode rejection), with scrollsSideways counting input and textarea fields; delivered through subscribeMouseNavigate like nav:swipe.

nodes.name: SN-03.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-03 (partial): manual Windows release-criteria check on a Precision Touchpad — iterative user testing across SN-05..SN-09 drove the reliability fixes; swipes are confirmed working with SN-09, but sideways scrolling and mouse cases are not yet reported.

nodes.name: SN-04.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-04 (partial): manual Linux release-criteria check — one Wayland trace confirmed GTK scroll-begin/scroll-end semantics and exposed replayed scrolls; the remaining criteria, X11 and mouse cases are still pending.

nodes.name: SN-05.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-05: make swipes in a row each navigate — SwipeGuard splits the wheel stream into strokes with a speed decay-and-rise rule so one swipe's momentum no longer swallows the next.

nodes.name: SN-06.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-06: one swipe, one step — stricter stroke splitting that requires a finger let-go on Windows (three falling events at a quarter peak) and scroll-begin/scroll-end gesture bounds on Linux, validated with a 1000-swipe simulation table.

nodes.name: SN-07.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-07: skip GTK's replayed scroll copies in mousenav_linux.c via event-time dedup so one swipe sends nav:swipe once, and add the AGENT_SESSIONS_TRACE_NAV trace switch for touchpad debugging without a rebuild.

nodes.name: SN-08.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-08 (superseded): drop strokes for a 200 ms gesture gap plus a 500 ms post-swipe cooldown on Windows; real touchpad streams still mis-stepped, so SN-09 and SN-10 replaced the page detector with native touchpad reading.

nodes.name: SN-09.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-09: read the Precision Touchpad natively on Windows — internal/touchswipe turns HID Raw Input reports into at most one swipe per touch, dispatched as nav:swipe to the window under the cursor via mousenav_windows.go, with layout tests against real touchpads.

nodes.name: SN-10.md
nodes.summary: Task SN-10: remove the page's wheel-based swipe detector now that Windows sends nav:swipe natively — SwipeGuard only tracks whether the current gesture scrolled something sideways, and drops nav:swipe while it did.

nodes.name: SW-01.md
nodes.summary: Task SW-01 (partial): macOS native swipe detection in mousenav_darwin.m — the scroll-event monitor sums phased two-finger movement and calls goSwipeNavigate once at 80 points when the system Swipe-between-pages setting is on; the ObjC is not yet compiled on macOS.
