nodes.name: about.html
nodes.summary: HTML shell for the desktop app's About window, with a strict Content-Security-Policy that permits Wails IPC, mounting the about.ts entry module into #app.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Main HTML shell for the Agent Sessions desktop UI; sets a strict Content-Security-Policy allowing only self and Wails IPC connections, and loads src/main.ts as the Vite entry module.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the Svelte 5 + Vite frontend, defining dev/build/check scripts, a Node test runner using a custom loader, and dependencies such as CodeMirror, xterm.js, the Wails runtime, marked, DOMPurify and mermaid.

nodes.name: tsconfig.json
nodes.summary: TypeScript configuration extending @tsconfig/svelte, targeting ESNext with JS type-checking and isolated modules for all .ts, .js, .d.ts and .svelte sources under src.

nodes.name: publish-aur.sh
nodes.summary: Commits a verified agent-sessions-bin package (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, LICENSE) to a clone of its AUR git repository on master, after checking the .SRCINFO matches the PKGBUILD, the origin is the right AUR repo and the checkout is clean; pushes only with --push.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash with set -euo pipefail; uses git -C plumbing (rev-parse --verify, merge-base --is-ancestor, rev-list --count) to safely fast-forward and detect unpushed commits.

nodes.name: render-pkgbuild.sh
nodes.summary: Renders the agent-sessions-bin AUR PKGBUILD from PKGBUILD.in for a stable release, filling version, pkgrel and the amd64/arm64 .deb and LICENSE SHA-256 checksums taken from the release's SHA256SUMS, and copies the LICENSE into the output directory.
nodes.languageNotes: Placeholder substitution via sed with a final grep guard for unfilled @TOKEN@ markers; awk strips sha256sum's '*' binary-mode prefix.

nodes.name: verify-aur-package.sh
nodes.summary: Verifies a rendered agent-sessions-bin package inside a throwaway Arch Linux Docker container: generates .SRCINFO, builds with makepkg, checks the aarch64 checksum, runs namcap, installs with pacman, validates shared libraries, desktop entry, icon, license and remote server bundles, then confirms clean removal.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs a heredoc script inside docker with a 1200s timeout; builds as an unprivileged user via runuser and swaps CARCH in makepkg.conf to verify the other architecture's source.

nodes.name: assemble-rpm-repo.sh
nodes.summary: Test helper that assembles dnf repodata (primary, filelists, other and repomd.xml) in an output directory from the rpm entries of repo-meta.json files, mirroring what the website Worker builds, so dnf repoquery can run on it.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Writes one gzipped createrepo_c XML file by concatenating a given field of every rpm entry from the repo-meta.json inputs between its header and footer.

nodes.name: notify-ingest.sh
nodes.summary: Release workflow step that POSTs a published release tag to the website ingest API so the apt and dnf repositories are rebuilt, with input validation, a token passed via file, and retries on network errors, 404 and 5xx.

nodes.name: repo-keys.sh
nodes.summary: Offline key-management CLI for the Linux repositories' two Ed25519 signing keys (repo and RPM): creates, extends, shows, exports, backs up and restores them in a dedicated GnuPG home.
nodes.languageNotes: Dispatches subcommands to cmd_* functions and wraps gpg in a helper g that pins GNUPGHOME; uses umask 077 subshells to protect secret files.

nodes.name: write_files
nodes.summary: Exports a key's public part, secret part and revocation certificate into <role>-<keyID>.*.asc files in the key directory.

nodes.name: show
nodes.summary: Lists each secret key's fingerprint, user ID, creation and expiry dates, and when to renew or replace it.

nodes.name: cmd_new
nodes.summary: Generates a new 3-year Ed25519 signing key for the repo or RPM role, checks it and writes its files.

nodes.name: cmd_extend
nodes.summary: Extends a repository key by another validity period, refusing RPM keys which must be rotated instead.

nodes.name: cmd_secret
nodes.summary: Prints the armored secret keys for the given fingerprints in order, for the REPO_SIGNING_KEY or RPM_SIGNING_KEY secrets.

nodes.name: cmd_backup
nodes.summary: Archives the key directory and encrypts it with an AES256 passphrase via gpg symmetric encryption.

nodes.name: cmd_restore
nodes.summary: Decrypts a key backup into a new directory and shows the restored keys.

nodes.name: repo-meta.sh
nodes.summary: Generates DIST_DIR/repo-meta.json: per-package apt Packages stanzas and createrepo_c primary/filelists/other XML elements for each .deb and .rpm of a release, consumed by the website Worker that builds the apt and dnf repositories.

nodes.name: sign-rpms.sh
nodes.summary: Signs every .rpm in a directory in place with the RPM signing key from RPM_SIGNING_KEY using a throwaway GnuPG home, then verifies each signature against that key alone.

nodes.name: test-repo-meta-fedora.sh
nodes.summary: Fedora half of make test-repo-meta: in a Fedora container, checks that dnf reads the assembled repository, Fedora's createrepo_c yields identical rpm entries, and repo-meta.sh handles signed packages correctly.

nodes.name: test-repo-meta.sh
nodes.summary: Test suite for repo-meta.sh and the repo-meta.json checks of release-checksums.sh against a real release's .deb and .rpm files; compares output with apt-ftparchive and createrepo_c and optionally leaves an assembled dnf repo for the Fedora test.

nodes.name: release_set
nodes.summary: Builds a fake release directory with the packages, repo-meta.json, stand-in installers and remote server archives plus SHA256SUMS for release-checksums tests.

nodes.name: expect_refused
nodes.summary: Asserts release-checksums.sh rejects the current release set with the expected error message.

nodes.name: verify-deb-install.sh
nodes.summary: Installs a .deb with apt in a clean throwaway Docker container and checks dependency resolution, shared-library linkage, installed file locations and clean purge.

nodes.name: verify-packages.sh
nodes.summary: Checks the .deb and .rpm produced by make package-linux without installing them: metadata, runtime dependencies from nfpm.yaml, exact file lists and modes, and byte-identical payloads including the desktop binary and remote servers.

nodes.name: depends_of
nodes.summary: Extracts the declared runtime dependencies for a package format from the overrides section of packaging/nfpm.yaml.

nodes.name: verify-repo.sh
nodes.summary: End-to-end check of the published apt and dnf repositories at a base URL: runs the documented setup, install, upgrade and removal commands in parallel clean containers and verifies the listed versions.

nodes.name: phase1
nodes.summary: Starts a container for an image and runs the documented prep and setup commands (plus the initial dnf install) for apt or dnf.

nodes.name: entitlements.plist
nodes.summary: Hardened-runtime entitlements for the Developer ID signed macOS app, granting only the Apple Events automation entitlement so Open in terminal can drive Terminal, iTerm2 and Ghostty via osascript.
nodes.languageNotes: Under the hardened runtime, Apple Events are refused with error -1743 unless this entitlement is present; no JIT exceptions are needed because WKWebView runs JavaScript in WebKit's own processes.

nodes.name: notarize.sh
nodes.summary: Submits a signed .dmg to Apple's notary service using a stored notarytool keychain profile, trusts only the JSON status (printing Apple's log on rejection), then staples and validates the ticket.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash array for auth flags avoids secrets on the command line; status is parsed with jq because notarytool may exit 0 for rejected submissions.

nodes.name: verify-dmg.sh
nodes.summary: Verifies the macOS .dmg produced by make package-macos without launching the app: image checksum, layout, universal arm64/x86_64 executable and minimum OS, Info.plist values, ad-hoc or Developer ID signatures with hardened runtime and entitlements, optional notarization/Gatekeeper checks, and the bundled remote servers.
nodes.languageNotes: Mounts the image read-only into a temp dir with a trap-based retrying detach for cleanup; signature checks grep codesign -d output line by line.

nodes.name: nfpm.yaml
nodes.summary: nfpm configuration for the Linux .deb and .rpm packages: installs the desktop binary, .desktop entry, icon and the gzipped remote servers for every platform, and declares GTK 4 / WebKitGTK 6.0 runtime dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: VERSION and ARCH are substituted from the environment by nfpm at package time; a glob src makes dst a directory.

nodes.name: release-checksums.sh
nodes.summary: Release-time check that a merged artifact directory holds exactly the expected set of .deb/.rpm/.dmg/.msi/setup.exe/server archives and repo-meta.json for a version, verifies the servers survived transit, then writes an aggregate SHA256SUMS.

nodes.name: verify-remote-servers.sh
nodes.summary: Validates a directory of gzipped headless remote servers: one archive per REMOTE_PLATFORMS entry from the Makefile, each a sound gzip with a 64-bit executable for its OS/arch, with optional SHA256SUMS matching and a host run checking the version handshake.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Guide to the Windows installer: per-user install, update and recovery behaviour, building the MSI and GUI setup wrapper, the fullscreen compatibility custom action default, and validation steps.

nodes.name: build-setup.sh
nodes.summary: Builds the Windows GUI setup wrapper exe that embeds a given MSI: stages the setup Go sources plus internal/winmsi in a temp dir, compiles an asInvoker manifest with windres, and cross-compiles without touching the source tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Strips release suffixes from VERSION because Windows Installer compares only the numeric ProductVersion.

nodes.name: conpty-LICENSE.txt
nodes.summary: Microsoft MIT license text shipped alongside the bundled ConPTY files used by the terminal panel on Windows.

nodes.name: verify-packages.sh
nodes.summary: Statically inspects the built .msi and _setup.exe: MSI summary, properties, UpgradeCode, upgrade rules, compatibility custom actions and order, WebView2 condition, shortcuts and extracted payload layout, plus a 64-bit asInvoker setup exe embedding the exact MSI.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses msitools (msiinfo, msiextract) and mingw objdump so Windows packages can be checked from Linux CI.

nodes.name: .gitattributes
nodes.summary: Git attributes forcing LF line endings for all text files on every platform so golden files and fixtures compare byte for byte, including on Windows.

nodes.name: action.yml
nodes.summary: Composite GitHub Action that installs Ubuntu packages via install.sh, keying a monthly per-OS/arch/package-set cache of downloaded .deb files and saving it only when a download happened.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses split actions/cache/restore and actions/cache/save steps with a never-matching primary key so restore-keys pick the newest cache while each download saves a fresh one.

nodes.name: install.sh
nodes.summary: Bash helper for the apt-install action: skips already-installed packages, installs from cached .debs when they cover the request, otherwise reorders the runner's apt mirror list to prefer Canonical's archive over Azure's, downloads and caches the .debs and signals save=true.

nodes.name: NOTICE
nodes.summary: Legal notice stating the PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 license, commercial-licensing contact, trademark terms and third-party asset licenses (vscode-icons, Lucide, ConPTY).

nodes.name: appid.go
nodes.summary: Defines the Linux GTK application id and GLib program name so desktop environments match windows to the packaged .desktop entry and WebKit keeps localStorage in a stable directory.

nodes.name: fonts_linux.go
nodes.summary: Linux cgo shim that disables GTK font hinting on the GTK main loop so WebKitGTK renders evenly spaced text under fractional scaling.

nodes.name: fonts_other.go
nodes.summary: No-op disableFontHinting for non-Linux desktop builds.

nodes.name: mousenav.go
nodes.summary: Shared desktop navigation plumbing: Wails event names for mouse side-button and touchpad-swipe back/forward, an env-controlled native trace logger, and dispatchNavigation which emits the event to a window.

nodes.name: mousenav_darwin.m
nodes.summary: macOS Objective-C NSEvent monitor that captures mouse side buttons 3/4 and recognises two-finger trackpad swipes from scroll phases, forwarding back/forward to Go via cgo exports.

nodes.name: mousenav_linux.c
nodes.summary: GTK4/WebKitGTK C code that hooks each window's web view with click and scroll controllers to turn mouse side buttons and two-finger touchpad swipes into back/forward navigation calls into Go, skipping replayed scrolls.

nodes.name: mousenav_native.go
nodes.summary: cgo bridge for Linux and macOS that installs the native side-button/swipe hooks and exports goMouseNavigate/goSwipeNavigate callbacks which resolve the native window to a Wails window and dispatch navigation events.

nodes.name: mousenav_other.go
nodes.summary: No-op mouse navigation hooks for desktop platforms other than Linux, macOS and Windows.

nodes.name: mousenav_windows.go
nodes.summary: Windows Precision Touchpad swipe detection: a message-only window on a locked OS thread reads Raw Input HID reports via user32/hid.dll, parses contact coordinates, feeds them to internal/touchswipe and dispatches swipe navigation to the app window under the cursor.
nodes.languageNotes: Calls Win32 and HID APIs through golang.org/x/sys/windows lazy DLL procs with hand-laid structs mirroring C layouts (WNDCLASSEXW, RAWINPUTHEADER, HIDP_CAPS).

nodes.name: print_darwin.m
nodes.summary: macOS Objective-C printing support that finds the window's WKWebView and runs an NSPrintOperation with the requested paper size, orientation and margins.

nodes.name: print_linux.c
nodes.summary: GTK4/WebKitGTK C printing support that locates the window's web view and runs an asynchronous WebKitPrintOperation with letter/A4 size, orientation and margins, holding references until printing finishes.

nodes.name: run_stub.go
nodes.summary: Fallback run entry point for builds without the desktop tag; prints an error and exits so plain go build/test succeed without GTK headers.

nodes.name: siri_darwin.go
nodes.summary: cgo wrapper that calls the Objective-C hook hiding macOS 27's Siri writing-tools button on the app's web views.

nodes.name: siri_darwin.m
nodes.summary: Objective-C runtime patch replacing WKWebView's allowsWritingToolsAffordance with NO so the Siri button no longer floats over the terminal prompt.

nodes.name: siri_other.go
nodes.summary: No-op hideSiriAffordance for non-macOS desktop builds.

nodes.name: terminal_fonts_darwin.go
nodes.summary: macOS cgo wrapper that returns installed monospace font families for the terminal panel from the CoreText helper.

nodes.name: terminal_fonts_darwin.m
nodes.summary: CoreText code that enumerates every installed font face and collects family names that are monospace or have fixed-advance printable ASCII (covering patched Nerd Fonts).

nodes.name: terminal_fonts_linux.go
nodes.summary: Lists terminal-suitable font families on Linux by querying fontconfig's fc-list for mono and dual-width spacing.

nodes.name: terminal_fonts_windows.go

nodes.name: sshtest.go
nodes.summary: Test-only helper that runs a throwaway OpenSSH server in Docker with users for sh, zsh, fish and tcsh login shells, pinned keys and network fault injection, and builds gzipped server bundles for the opt-in SSH integration tests.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds the Docker image once per process with sync.Once and uses testing.TB cleanup hooks to remove containers, keys and control sockets.

nodes.name: Host
nodes.summary: A running test container with its ssh config file, control path and per-user aliases.

nodes.name: Alias
nodes.summary: Returns the ssh alias for a remote user.

nodes.name: Start
nodes.summary: Builds the test image, starts a fresh container on a random localhost port, generates client and host keys, writes ssh config and known_hosts, and waits until sshd accepts logins; registers cleanup.

nodes.name: waitReady
nodes.summary: Retries a plain ssh login until sshd in the container is up or the test fails.

nodes.name: Exec
nodes.summary: Runs a shell script in the container as root and returns stdout.

nodes.name: ExecAs
nodes.summary: Runs a shell script in the container as a given user and returns stdout.

nodes.name: CutNetwork
nodes.summary: Adds iptables rules that silently drop all ssh traffic so open connections hang as on a lost network.

nodes.name: RestoreNetwork
nodes.summary: Removes the iptables rules added by CutNetwork.

nodes.name: Pause
nodes.summary: Freezes every process in the container to simulate a hung host.

nodes.name: Unpause
nodes.summary: Resumes a container paused by Pause.

nodes.name: CopyTree
nodes.summary: Copies a local directory into a user home in the container and sets its ownership.

nodes.name: ServerBundleDir
nodes.summary: Builds and caches, once per version, a gzipped linux agent-sessions-cli bundle like make remote-servers and returns its directory for AGENT_SESSIONS_REMOTE_SERVERS_DIR.

nodes.name: buildBundle
nodes.summary: Cross-compiles agent-sessions-cli for linux with the version stamped into a per-user, per-version temp directory, gzips it and renames the archive into place so parallel test processes can share it.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs an external command and returns its combined output with a descriptive error on failure.

nodes.name: golden.go
nodes.summary: Golden-file test helpers that register a -update flag and compare JSON or text output against testdata/golden files, printing a unified diff on mismatch.

nodes.name: JSON
nodes.summary: Indent-marshals a value and compares it with testdata/golden/<name>.json, rewriting the file when -update is set and failing with a unified diff otherwise.

nodes.name: Text
nodes.summary: Compares a text result with a golden file, rewriting it under -update and reporting a unified diff on mismatch.

nodes.name: Marshal
nodes.summary: Encodes a value as two-space-indented JSON without HTML escaping, the canonical golden-file form.

nodes.name: platform.go
nodes.summary: Cross-platform test helpers that let one test suite run on Linux, macOS and Windows by resolving temp-dir paths and skipping checks an OS cannot support (symlinks, mode bits, missing commands).

nodes.name: TempDir
nodes.summary: Returns t.TempDir() with symlinks and Windows 8.3 short names resolved, matching the normalized paths production code reports.

nodes.name: Symlink
nodes.summary: Creates a symlink for a test, skipping the test when the OS or account lacks symlink privilege instead of failing.

nodes.name: SkipWithoutModeBits
nodes.summary: Skips the test on platforms such as Windows where file permission bits are not enforced.

nodes.name: RequireCommand
nodes.summary: Skips the test when a required external command is not found on PATH.

nodes.name: touchswipe.go
nodes.summary: Detects two-finger horizontal swipes from Precision Touchpad contact frames (Windows Raw Input), converting HID logical units to millimetres and emitting at most one Back/Forward step per touch.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure, platform-independent Go state machine fed by the Windows Raw Input reader, so the gesture logic is testable without a touchpad.

nodes.name: String
nodes.summary: Returns the readable name of a swipe Direction (None, Back or Forward).

nodes.name: Contact
nodes.summary: One touchpad contact in a frame: its contact id, position and whether it is touching.

nodes.name: Frames
nodes.summary: Accumulates contact reports from Raw Input until a full frame of the declared contact count has arrived.

nodes.name: Report
nodes.summary: Adds one Raw Input report's contacts to the pending frame and returns the completed frame once all contacts are in.

nodes.name: Tracker
nodes.summary: Per-touch state machine that tracks the start position of two fingers and decides whether the touch becomes a sideways swipe or a scroll.

nodes.name: Frame
nodes.summary: Feeds one contact frame into the tracker, ending lost or lifted touches and returning a swipe Direction once two fingers move far enough sideways before moving vertically.

nodes.name: Down
nodes.summary: Reports whether a touch is currently in progress.

nodes.name: HIDAxis
nodes.summary: Describes a HID touchpad axis (logical range, physical unit and exponent) used to convert coordinates to millimetres.

nodes.name: mmPerUnit
nodes.summary: Computes millimetres per logical unit from a HID axis's unit code and exponent, returning false when the descriptor is unusable.

nodes.name: Scales
nodes.summary: Returns the X and Y millimetre-per-unit scales for a touchpad, falling back to a default width when the device reports no usable size.

nodes.name: PKGBUILD.in
nodes.summary: Template for the Arch Linux agent-sessions-bin PKGBUILD that repackages the released .deb for x86_64 and aarch64, with version and SHA-256 placeholders filled by render-pkgbuild.sh.

nodes.name: io.github.ginkcode.AgentSessions.desktop
nodes.summary: freedesktop.org desktop entry that registers Agent Sessions in Linux application menus with its icon, categories and search keywords.

nodes.name: Info.plist.in
nodes.summary: Info.plist template for the macOS app bundle, with product name, version, minimum macOS and copyright placeholders filled by make package-macos; keeps the Wails v2 bundle identifier so granted permissions persist.

nodes.name: agent-sessions.exe.manifest
nodes.summary: Windows application manifest for agent-sessions.exe enabling Common Controls v6, per-monitor-v2 DPI awareness and asInvoker execution level, with the version filled in by make windows-app.

nodes.name: agent-sessions.wxs
nodes.summary: WiX installer definition for a per-user MSI that installs the app, gzipped remote servers and ConPTY under LocalAppData, adds shortcuts, checks for WebView2 and schedules the AppCompat custom actions.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses immediate/rollback/deferred custom-action ordering so registry changes made by the native DLL are undone if the install fails.

nodes.name: appcompat-ca.c
nodes.summary: Native x64 MSI custom-action DLL that snapshots, rewrites and rolls back the per-user AppCompatFlags Layers registry value for the installed agent-sessions.exe, with a platform-independent tokenizer and snapshot codec that tests can compile alone.
nodes.languageNotes: Guarded by APPCOMPAT_CORE_TEST so the pure parsing/codec half compiles without Windows headers; production entry points use __declspec(dllexport) WINAPI.

nodes.name: target_token
nodes.summary: Case-insensitively checks whether a Layers token is the compatibility flag this custom action manages.

nodes.name: registry_text
nodes.summary: Converts a snapshot's raw REG_SZ bytes into a NUL-terminated wide string, rejecting malformed data.

nodes.name: layer_value
nodes.summary: Computes the new Layers value by tokenizing the snapshot, dropping or adding the managed flag for uninstall or install, and reporting whether the value should remain.

nodes.name: snapshot_encode
nodes.summary: Encodes a registry snapshot (path, existence, remove flag, bytes) into a hex CustomActionData string.

nodes.name: snapshot_decode
nodes.summary: Parses and validates an encoded CustomActionData snapshot back into a Snapshot structure.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Logs a failed custom-action operation with its error code to the MSI log and returns install failure.

nodes.name: property
nodes.summary: Reads an MSI property into a newly allocated wide string, growing the buffer as needed.

nodes.name: read_snapshot
nodes.summary: Reads the current Layers registry value for the target path into a snapshot, recording whether it exists.

nodes.name: write_value
nodes.summary: Writes or deletes the Layers registry value for the target executable path.

nodes.name: PrepareAppCompat
nodes.summary: Immediate custom action that reads the install path and remove flag, snapshots the registry, validates the transformation and stores the encoded snapshot for the rollback and deferred actions.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Shared deferred/rollback body: decodes the snapshot, verifies the registry still matches it, then applies the new Layers value or restores the original.

nodes.name: ApplyAppCompat
nodes.summary: Deferred custom-action entry point that applies the Layers change.

nodes.name: RollbackAppCompat
nodes.summary: Rollback custom-action entry point that restores the original Layers value.

nodes.name: appcompat-ca-test.c
nodes.summary: Standalone C test program that includes appcompat-ca.c in core-test mode and exercises the Layers tokenizer and snapshot codec with assertions under ASan/UBSan, no Windows SDK needed.

nodes.name: snapshot
nodes.summary: Builds a test Snapshot with a Unicode-heavy path and UTF-16LE registry bytes for the given text.

nodes.name: layers
nodes.summary: Asserts that layer_value turns a given Layers string into the expected result and presence flag.

nodes.name: roundtrip
nodes.summary: Asserts that a snapshot survives snapshot_encode followed by snapshot_decode unchanged.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the tokenizer cases, codec round trips and malformed-input rejection checks, printing ok on success.

nodes.name: bundled_windows.go

nodes.name: unbundled_windows.go

nodes.name: main_windows.go

nodes.languageNotes: Calls Win32 APIs through golang.org/x/sys/windows lazy DLL procs and the registry package instead of cgo.

nodes.name: windowsPlatform
nodes.summary: Real Windows implementation of the setup platform interface, holding the user SID, system msiexec path, recovery directory and log file.

nodes.name: setupMain
nodes.summary: Validates the bundled MSI, resolves the non-elevated user identity, takes the setup mutex, locates msiexec and runs the guided setup flow in the wizard, returning the process exit code.

nodes.name: currentIdentity
nodes.summary: Refuses to run elevated and returns the current user's SID string.

nodes.name: acquireSetupMutex
nodes.summary: Creates a per-user named mutex so only one setup instance runs at a time.

nodes.name: systemMSIExec
nodes.summary: Locates and validates msiexec.exe in the system directory.

nodes.name: CurrentSID
nodes.summary: Returns the current user's SID.

nodes.name: Discover
nodes.summary: Lists installed Agent Sessions products for the setup flow.

nodes.name: Confirm
nodes.summary: Asks the user to confirm the installation via a message box.

nodes.name: RetryClose
nodes.summary: Asks the user to close the running app and retry.

nodes.name: Running
nodes.summary: Reports whether Agent Sessions is currently running for this user.

nodes.name: LogPath
nodes.summary: Returns the path of a named log file in the recovery directory.

nodes.name: Trace
nodes.summary: Appends a timestamped line to the setup log.

nodes.name: Prepare
nodes.summary: Verifies the bundled MSI checksum, creates a per-user recovery directory with the MSI and log, validates the package and returns the payload with its product code.

nodes.name: Prerequisite
nodes.summary: Checks the registry for the WebView2 runtime and returns an error when it is missing.

nodes.name: Execute
nodes.summary: Runs one msiexec transaction (install or uninstall) with logging and returns its exit status.

nodes.name: appRunning
nodes.summary: Enumerates processes to detect whether agent-sessions.exe from the install directory runs in the current user's session.

nodes.name: inspectAppProcess
nodes.summary: Opens a process and checks that its image path and owner match the installed app and current user.

nodes.name: wizard.go
nodes.summary: Platform-neutral wizard layer for setup: a wizardView interface and a guidedPlatform decorator that reports progress and asks questions through the wizard while runSetup keeps all consent and transaction logic.

nodes.name: wizardView
nodes.summary: Interface the setup worker uses to show status text and ask consent or close-app questions on the UI thread.

nodes.name: guidedPlatform
nodes.summary: Decorator over the setup platform that adds wizard progress messages and routes confirmations to the wizard view.

nodes.name: Prepare
nodes.summary: Shows a preparing message and delegates payload preparation to the wrapped platform.

nodes.name: Confirm
nodes.summary: Asks the consent question through the wizard view.

nodes.name: RetryClose
nodes.summary: Asks through the wizard whether to retry after the user closes the app.

nodes.name: Execute
nodes.summary: Shows the installing or uninstalling status and delegates the MSI transaction to the wrapped platform.

nodes.name: resultTitle
nodes.summary: Chooses the wizard's final-page title from the setup outcome.

nodes.name: finishText
nodes.summary: Builds the final status text for a setup outcome, including exit status and recovery directory.

nodes.name: wizard_state.go
nodes.summary: Platform-independent navigation rules for the setup wizard (pages, started/finished state, Next delay) kept separate from Win32 code so they can be unit-tested.

nodes.name: wizardNavigation

nodes.name: wizard_windows.go
nodes.summary: Native Win32 implementation of the setup wizard window: creates controls, handles DPI and high-contrast graphics, marshals worker events to the UI thread and drives Next/Back/Cancel through the window procedure.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds a Win32 GUI directly via lazy user32/gdi32/comctl32 procs and windows.NewCallback, with the message loop pinned to one OS thread by runtime.LockOSThread.

nodes.name: nativeWizard
nodes.summary: Win32 wizard window state: handles, fonts, navigation, pending questions and a mutex-guarded event queue between the setup worker and UI thread.

nodes.name: post
nodes.summary: Queues an event from the worker and wakes the UI thread with a posted window message.

nodes.name: Show
nodes.summary: Posts a status page update from the setup worker to the wizard UI.

nodes.name: Ask
nodes.summary: Posts a question to the UI thread and blocks the worker until the user answers.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: On the UI thread, applies queued worker events: status pages, questions and the final result.

nodes.name: runWizard
nodes.summary: Registers the window class, creates the wizard window and runs the message loop on a locked OS thread, starting the setup worker and waiting for it before returning its outcome.

nodes.name: createControls
nodes.summary: Creates the wizard's static text and Back/Next/Cancel button controls.

nodes.name: releaseGraphics
nodes.summary: Frees the wizard's GDI fonts, brushes and icon handles.

nodes.name: refreshGraphics

nodes.name: layout
nodes.summary: Positions the wizard's controls for the current client size and DPI scale.

nodes.name: showQuestion
nodes.summary: Displays a pending question page and delays enabling Next to avoid accidental confirmation.

nodes.name: buttons
nodes.summary: Updates the labels and enabled state of the Back, Next and Cancel buttons for the current page.

nodes.name: answer
nodes.summary: Delivers the user's answer to the waiting worker and returns to the working page.

nodes.name: nextAction
nodes.summary: Handles Next: starts the setup worker on first consent, answers a pending question, or closes after the result.

nodes.name: cancelAction
nodes.summary: Handles Cancel or window close: declines a pending question or closes when no work is running.

nodes.name: windowProc

nodes.name: qa-perf-bench.sh
nodes.summary: QA and performance benchmark script that builds the CLI if needed, then times a cold full scan (target under 5 s) and the largest session's load (target under 1 s) on real local data and prints provider breakdowns and diagnostics.

nodes.name: repair-codex-rollouts.py
nodes.summary: Offline POSIX repair tool that renames legacy rollout-restored Codex rollout files to canonical names and updates the SQLite state and JSON session index, previewing by default and applying with backups, locking and conflict checks.
nodes.languageNotes: Standard-library only; uses ExitStack and atomic temp-file writes so a partial failure leaves both old and new paths valid for a rerun.

nodes.name: check_path
nodes.summary: Rejects symlinks below the resolved Codex root and checks the path is a regular file.

nodes.name: identity
nodes.summary: Returns a file's device, inode, size and mtime so later steps can detect changes since preview.

nodes.name: canonical_name
nodes.summary: Reads a rollout's session_meta line and derives its canonical rollout-<timestamp>-<id>.jsonl name, refusing mismatched ids or missing timestamps.

nodes.name: connect
nodes.summary: Opens a SQLite database through a file URI.

nodes.name: has_paths
nodes.summary: Checks whether a SQLite table has the id and rollout_path columns.

nodes.name: index_data
nodes.summary: Rewrites legacy rollout paths inside the JSONL session index for the planned repairs.

nodes.name: validate_rows
nodes.summary: Verifies SQLite thread rows still point at the expected legacy paths before mutation.

nodes.name: plan
nodes.summary: Scans the Codex sessions tree for legacy rollout files and builds the list of repairs with their targets, database and index entries.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Applies planned repairs under a writer lock: backs up the databases and index, renames files without overwriting, updates SQLite rows and the index, and refuses changed or aliased inputs.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI arguments, prints the repair plan and applies it only with --apply.

nodes.name: test_repair_codex_rollouts.py
nodes.summary: unittest suite for repair-codex-rollouts.py that builds synthetic Codex homes and checks preview, apply, backups, conflict and symlink refusal, lock handling, partial-failure recovery and native resume after repair.

nodes.name: RepairTests
nodes.summary: Tests the repair tool's preview and apply paths against a synthetic rollout, SQLite state and session index, covering backups, conflicts, aliasing, locks and partial failures.

nodes.name: NativeResumeTests
nodes.summary: Checks that a repaired paginated rollout can still be resumed by id with the native Codex client.

project.name: agent-sessions
project.description: Agent Sessions is a desktop workspace (Go + Wails backend, Svelte/TypeScript frontend) with a companion CLI and remote servers for finding, following and resuming coding-agent sessions from Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode, locally, in WSL and over SSH. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

layers.name: Desktop UI
layers.description: Svelte and TypeScript presentation, reactive state, desktop API adapters, transcript rendering, editor and terminal views, with frontend assets, build settings and tests.

layers.name: Desktop and CLI Application
layers.description: Wails desktop and CLI entry points compose the headless engine, expose frontend bindings, route local and remote operations, and integrate native windows, menus and touch gestures.

layers.name: Session Workflow Services
layers.description: The headless engine orchestrates session browsing and mutation, portable bundles, cross-agent handoffs, translation, navigation grouping and Codex rollout repair.

layers.name: Session Providers and Index
layers.description: Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode adapters normalize native histories into shared models, discover and watch sessions, and persist the searchable SQLite catalog and FTS schema.

layers.name: Agent Runtime and Managed Tools
layers.description: ACP clients, Codex daemon bridging, chat attachments, agent launch commands and verified tool installations run coding agents and language servers with controlled process trees and login environments.

layers.name: Remote and Terminal Transport
layers.description: SSH and WSL host deployment, JSON-RPC clients and stdio servers carry engine operations and events across hosts, while platform PTY adapters support interactive terminals.

layers.name: Workspace Files and Code Intelligence
layers.description: Rooted file operations, Git inspection and editing, language-server diagnostics and saved-file checkers power project file, editor and repository workflows.

layers.name: Shared Safety and Test Utilities
layers.description: Common path resolution, JSONL streaming, secret redaction, atomic configuration editing, file locking and deterministic fixture helpers support safe cross-platform session processing.

layers.name: Build, Release and Platform Support
layers.description: Go and Wails project configuration, Make targets, CI/CD, signed releases, cross-platform installers, update verification and performance automation build and distribute Agent Sessions.

layers.name: Documentation and Project Governance
layers.description: Product and storage-format references, feature plans, milestone task records, repair runbooks, contributor instructions and bundled license notices document Agent Sessions and its delivery history.

tour.title: A Local-First Session Workspace
tour.description: Start with the README to understand Agent Sessions as a desktop companion for the histories that Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode already save. It brings browsing, search, resume, handoffs and project tools into one workspace across local, WSL and SSH environments, without requiring an Agent Sessions account or central server. Keep its distinction between read-only browsing and explicit modifying actions in mind throughout the tour.

tour.title: Desktop and CLI Entrypoints
tour.description: With the product boundary established, compare the desktop main function with the companion CLI's subcommand dispatcher. The desktop entrypoint handles helper modes before launching Wails, while the CLI exposes operations such as scan, show, handoff and serve without a GUI. The widely connected App service is the desktop composition boundary: it wires the engine, exposes JavaScript bindings and routes operations to local or remote backends; go.mod records the Go module and runtime dependencies behind this structure.
tour.languageLesson: Go build constraints select which files participate in a build; the desktop entrypoint is guarded by the desktop build tag. A directory can therefore contain platform or application variants without compiling every file into every executable.

tour.title: Shared Models and Backend Contract
tour.description: Before following data through the entrypoints, learn the provider-neutral vocabulary in model.go: session references, metadata, messages, parts and transcripts. The frontend's central TypeScript types mirror backend payloads, making this shared vocabulary especially important at the language boundary. The context-first Backend interface separates callers from execution location, and the headless Engine implements it while owning scanning, indexing, watching and catalog events.
tour.languageLesson: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly: a type implements an interface by providing its methods, without an implements declaration. Here that lets the local engine and a remote RPC client present the same Backend contract to callers.

tour.title: Native Histories Become Transcripts
tour.description: Using Step 3's model, the Provider interface defines how agents expose detection, scanning, loading and launch-related behavior, while the registry constructs the supported providers. Read the verified storage-format reference alongside the Claude JSONL loader as one concrete example of converting native records into normalized messages, parts and tool calls. Its output clipping and lazy blob retrieval show why browsing need not eagerly materialize every large tool result or image.

tour.title: Discovery and Incremental Refresh
tour.description: Once providers can read native histories, the scan runner detects and scans them concurrently to populate the session catalog. The watcher converts filesystem activity into debounced, coalesced changes, and the index refresher coordinates incremental scans, database commits and catalog synchronization. The engine's cache coordination elects one SQLite writer while other engines read its database, explaining how multiple running engines share an index without each independently acting as its writer.

tour.title: SQLite Catalog and Search
tour.description: Step 5's refresh pipeline persists its results in a private SQLite cache whose database manager handles migrations, transactional scan commits and corruption recovery. The initial schema separates session metadata, provider scan state, a durable indexing queue and trigger-maintained FTS5 search data. The background worker loads transcripts outside write transactions, while search.go turns user queries into safe MATCH expressions and parameterized queries with snippets, keeping full-text indexing distinct from discovery.
tour.languageLesson: SQLite FTS5 virtual tables provide full-text retrieval rather than ordinary row filtering. An external-content design keeps searchable text in a companion table, with triggers maintaining the search index as that content changes.

tour.title: Frontend Bindings and Reactive State
tour.description: Now follow the indexed catalog back toward the desktop interface introduced in Step 2. appBinding.ts explicitly lists exposed Go methods, api.ts wraps those methods and backend events behind a typed API, and appState.svelte.ts maintains session-browser state in response to catalog changes. App.svelte composes the sidebar, session list, transcript and terminal panel and initializes the stores; the API's browser mock fallback separates UI development from the desktop runtime.

tour.title: Loading and Navigating Conversations
tour.description: Building on the catalog-driven UI, the GUI-independent Service supplies listing, filtering, grouping and message paging, while the transcript cache bounds memory and coordinates provider loads. TranscriptView consumes those conversations through paging, live refresh and navigation rather than requiring the entire history to remain visible at once. The session-search store adds debounced full-text queries and jump requests, connecting Step 6's indexed search to a specific place in the transcript.

tour.title: Resume, Chat and Terminal Execution
tour.description: After finding a conversation, the workflow can move from viewing saved history to actively running an agent. Engine launch methods prepare resume, new-session and handoff commands, while the chat manager owns sessions, queues prompts and brokers permission questions through the ACP client. The terminal manager is a separate execution path that runs processes in pseudo-terminals and streams output with flow-control acknowledgements, distinguishing terminal interaction from structured chat updates.

tour.title: Handoffs and Portable Session Bundles
tour.description: Beyond resuming the original agent in Step 9, handoffs build context from a session and its descendants for use by another agent. Export gathers native records and restores transcript fidelity for portable bundles, whose manifest describes source metadata, native files and redaction counts. The bundle reader checks archive names, manifest consistency and checksums, while the redaction module supplies secret and home-path scrubbing primitives; portability therefore has explicit integrity and privacy boundaries, not just serialization.

tour.title: One Backend Across Hosts
tour.description: Return to Step 3's Backend interface to see how the same workflows operate away from the desktop machine. The RPC client implements that interface by forwarding calls to a headless stdio server, which provides initialization, concurrent request handling and an idle timeout. SSH deployment installs a version-checked bundled server, while the connection store selects Local, WSL or SSH routes, tracks capabilities and resets dependent stores when the host changes.

tour.title: Project Files and Git Workflows
tour.description: With local and remote routing understood, explore the project workspace surrounding a session. The connected GoToFileDialog and FileViewer components combine file selection, previews, editing, Git views and navigation, while the content-search store coordinates project-wide search and replacement. On the backend, files.go supplies listings and content reads, and git_diff.go distinguishes working-tree-versus-index from index-versus-HEAD comparisons so the Changes pane can present the correct original and editable content.

tour.title: Connection-Scoped Code Intelligence
tour.description: Building on the editor and navigation in Step 12, the diagnostics manager owns attachments, approval, preparation and checker runs for one authenticated connection. The language-server session manager handles host-local processes with gated launch, capability negotiation, retries and capacity eviction. The frontend diagnostics store coordinates live document synchronization, navigation requests and result reconciliation, showing that code intelligence spans UI state and controlled backend process lifecycles rather than living only inside the editor.

tour.title: Guarding Destructive Session Actions
tour.description: Revisit the README's boundary between browsing and modification now that the main workflows are familiar. The management service uses HMAC-sealed preview tokens that deletion must revalidate, while its liveness guard refuses destructive actions on running or recently active sessions and fails closed when status is unknown. Path-safety checks also resolve containment and reject protected names, symlinks and special files, making preview authorization, process state and filesystem identity separate checks before native history can be changed.

tour.title: Build, Verify and Distribute
tour.description: Finish by connecting the runtime and safety boundaries to how the project is built and shipped. The frontend manifest defines Svelte/Vite development and check commands, wails.json supplies product metadata and the release version, and the Makefile coordinates tests, desktop builds, CLI builds, remote servers and platform packaging. CI exercises Go race tests, frontend checks and desktop builds across operating systems, while the release workflow builds installers and remote bundles, verifies artifacts and signs checksums before publishing.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows separate event triggers from jobs and ordered steps. Read ci.yml for the development verification path and release.yml for the publishing path: they encode different lifecycle responsibilities even when some checks overlap.
